name: whoami
description: Read site identity, actual capabilities, current shared policy and version drift. Claude owns source-backed strategy, research and draft preparation. Before changing a plugin setting use inspect_plugin_capability; after creating a workflow draft use verify_content_workflow. Missing GSC evidence does not block useful niche content.

name: render_probe

extract.description: Optional comma list: schema,links,images,headings. Default all four.

diff.description: Return ONLY the delta vs the previous probe of this post (kept 24h) — use for the AFTER probe of a verify cycle; unchanged facets collapse to counts.

description: Loopback-fetch a post's OWN rendered front end and introspect the live DOM — the reliable verify path when external curl is WAF-blocked (403). Returns: schema (every JSON-LD block, attributed to its emitter — Rank Math / hand-built snippet / cc-assistant — and linted for self-serving aggregateRating on org/business nodes, duplicate @id, duplicate BreadcrumbList, and breadcrumb items missing name), links (every <a> with its RESOLVED accessible name = link text OR child img[alt] OR aria-label, so an alt'd image link is NOT falsely reported empty), images (rendered alt coverage), and headings (the live h1-h6 outline). Use BEFORE and AFTER any edit to verify what actually shipped. Optional `extract` is a comma list: schema,links,images,headings (default all).

name: get_elementor_tree
description: Full nested-node tree of an Elementor page — EVERY node, not just roots (get_page_map) or leaf widgets (get_elementor_widgets). Each node: id, el_type, widget_type, depth, parent_id, position (index within its parent), path, child_count, a grid/flex layout hint, and a short label. Use this to reach MIDDLE containers (grid rows, column wrappers) by id without exporting + parsing the raw data, and to spot grid dead-rows (compare layout.grid_rows x layout.grid_columns against child_count).

name: schema_scan

post_ids.description: Optional comma list of post IDs. Omit to scan a representative sample (front page + most-recently-modified pages).

limit.description: Max pages to probe. Default 12, cap 40.

description: Site-wide schema-source scan: runs the render_probe schema lint across a sample of pages (or explicit post_ids) and aggregates every JSON-LD issue by emitter (Rank Math / hand-built snippet / cc-assistant) and check (self_serving_rating, breadcrumb_missing_name, duplicate_breadcrumb, invalid JSON). Catches the wrong-aggregateRating / broken-breadcrumb class everywhere at once — including emitters cc-assistant cannot itself edit (fix those at their source). Optional post_ids (comma list) targets specific pages; limit caps how many pages are probed (each is one loopback fetch, default 12, cap 40).

name: redirect_audit
description: Inspect configured redirect destinations and chains. A homepage destination is a candidate for relevance review, not evidence of diluted rankings. Verify purpose, destination content, language and dependencies before any redirect or retirement proposal.

name: managed_schema

post_id.description: Optional. Return the full raw JSON-LD for this one post; omit to list all posts with managed schema.

description: Read-only: show the JSON-LD that cc-assistant ITSELF injects at wp_head, and on which posts. Reads the per-post _cc_emergency_service_schema (data-cc-assistant="emergency-service") and _cc_assistant_schema_jsonld (data-cc-assistant="page-jsonld") postmeta written by propose_emergency_service_schema / propose_schema. Without args: lists every post carrying managed schema with parsed @type + byte size + the live enabled flags. With post_id: returns the full raw JSON-LD for that one post. Use this to audit the plugin's own schema output (it was previously invisible — a bulk-applied emergency-service node became a silent site-wide duplicate). Disable an emitter site-wide via option cc_assistant_emergency_schema_enabled / cc_assistant_page_schema_enabled (default true).

name: draft_rebuild_section

post_id.description: Post ID.

remove_id.description: Element id of the existing section to replace.

settings.description: Settings for the new root container (boxed width, bg, padding, etc.).

children.description: Pre-built child specs (widgets/containers), same shape as draft_add_elementor_container.

position.description: Optional insert position for the new section.

parent_id.description: Optional parent container id; empty = page root.

description: Atomically REBUILD a section: add a new container (with children) AND remove an old one as ONE all-or-nothing pending change. Replaces the draft_add_elementor_container + draft_remove_elementor_widget pair (and the "approve both together / mind the position drift" dance) — the page never shows a transient duplicate and never half-applies (a single read-modify-write; a pre-apply snapshot is the recovery point). No heading-duplicate guard, since replacing a section re-uses its headings by design. Args mirror draft_add_elementor_container (settings, children, position?, parent_id?, el_type?) plus remove_id = the existing section id to replace.

name: draft_add_section

post_id.description: Post ID.

data.description: Recipe content — see the tool description for each recipe's fields.

remove_id.description: Optional: atomically REPLACE this existing section instead of just adding.

description: Build a section from a semantic RECIPE — describe it by intent + content and the plugin expands the full brand-correct Elementor tree (eyebrow + 38px H2 + red accent bar, brand tokens, grid rows auto, FA5 icons, responsive type, capped widths). ~10 lines of data instead of ~300 lines of JSON. Queues via the proven apply path: container_add, or the atomic section_rebuild when remove_id is given. Recipes + their data fields: hero {eyebrow?, h1, sub?, ctas:[{text,href}], chips?:[string]}; card_grid {eyebrow?, heading, intro?, columns?, bg?, cta?:{text,href}, cards:[{title, description, icon?|image?, link?}]}; checklist_2col {eyebrow?, heading, intro?, bg?, icon?, items:[string]}; cta_banner {heading, sub?, ctas:[{text,href}]}; section_header {eyebrow?, heading, bg?}.

name: seo_playbook
description: Read current source-linked SEO rules from the shared agent contract, including niche growth, evidence, research, measurement and reviewed publication. The same rules are exposed in short form; heuristic scores do not supersede them.

name: health
description: Returns plugin health: pending changes count, snapshots count, Elementor status. Useful for a quick status check.

name: list_posts

post_type.description: Post type slug: "post", "page", or "any". Default: searches both posts and pages. Only types in the allowlist are accepted.

status.description: Post status: publish, draft, pending, private, future, any. Default "any".

description: Lists posts or pages from the connected WordPress site. Pagination supported.

name: get_post

slim.description: Skip body content and parsed Elementor tree. Default false.

widget_id.description: Optional Elementor widget id (8-char hex). When set, returns only that single widget instead of the full post.

description: Returns full details for a single post or page. Pass slim=true to drop the post_content body and the parsed Elementor tree (returns only metadata + content_length + elementor_size) when you only need to know structure. Pass widget_id="abcd1234" to fetch ONE widget node (id, settings, widgetType) instead of the whole post — much smaller, perfect for editing one text-editor without downloading 70KB of JSON.

name: get_elementor_widgets
description: Parses a post or page built with Elementor. Default summary returns headings, link counts/list, word count, and structure. Pass format="full" to also get every widget with its text, path, and meta (much larger). Returns has_elementor=false if the post has no Elementor data.

name: get_page_map

include_ascii.description: Include a plain-text ASCII tree of the map. Default true.

description: MANDATORY PRE-FLIGHT before any root-level draft_add_elementor_container. Returns the annotated, section-aware page map: every root container with its container_id, position, semantic label (auto-inferred from first H2), child widget types, and the "section pairs" the site visually presents (H2-alone container + its body container). The response also returns safe_insert_positions (gaps between complete sections) and risky_insert_positions (inside a pair). Calling this stamps a 10-minute transient — subsequent root container_add calls refuse with HTTP 422 if no recent map call exists, preventing inserts that split a logical section. Use include_ascii=true for a human-readable tree.

name: entity_lookup

q.description: Name or slug to search (matches post_title LIKE and post_name/slug).

description: Find a name or slug across ALL post types at once — product, page, post, Theme Builder templates, and any public CPT. Run this FIRST before building a new page for something, so you never build a duplicate of an entity that already exists as e.g. a WooCommerce product (a page-only list would miss it). Returns each match: id, title, slug, post_type, status, url, has_elementor, template_type (for templates), and exact_slug_match. exact_slug_match=true means that entity already owns the URL slug — edit it, do not build a duplicate.

name: layout_spec
description: Full normalized layout spec of an Elementor post: EVERY node (container + widget) with its path, structural position, type, child_count, and ALL settings — with volatile element/repeater ids stripped so it diffs cleanly against a clone. __globals__ kit-token refs are kept verbatim. Use to inspect one page in full; use layout_compare to diff two. Works on pages AND Theme Builder templates (e.g. a Single Product template).

name: layout_compare

reference_id.description: Reference post/template ID to match against.

description: Deep byte-level diff of two Elementor posts — the definitive "does my build match the reference" check, so a match is provable instead of eyeballed. Walks both trees in lockstep by structural position (element ids ignored) and returns EVERY delta: structural (missing_in_target / extra_in_target / widget-type mismatch) and per-setting value differences (path + setting key + target value vs reference value). Run it after any "make X match Y" build and fix deltas until match=true. Target and reference may each be a page OR a Theme Builder template (e.g. compare a product template to a machine page).

name: find_topic_clusters

limit.description: Max posts to scan. Default 200, cap 1000.

description: Find lexical TF-IDF relatedness clusters using weighted title, heading and body text. Similarity is a discovery signal, not proof of duplicates or harmful cannibalization. Use content_decision to inspect pairwise reader tasks before recommending changes.

name: analyze_topic_cluster

excerpt_chars.description: Body excerpt length per page. Default 500. Raise to 2000 for deeper read.

description: Read content observations for selected posts to compare reader tasks and inspect possible overlap. Similarity alone does not prove harmful cannibalization. Use content_decision before consolidation proposals.

name: list_pending_changes
description: Lists pending changes that Claude has proposed and are waiting for human approval. Use this to confirm what is in the queue before proposing more changes.

name: draft_update_post_meta

post_id.description: Post ID.

field.description: One of: post_title, post_excerpt, post_name, post_status, post_author. For post_author, value = user ID, login, email, or exact display name (resolved to an ID at queue time).

reasoning.description: Why this change makes sense. Shown to the reviewer.

dry_run.description: When true, return the validation result without queueing a pending row. No DB write.

success_metrics.description: Stated intent for outcome scoring. Most useful on post_title changes where CTR delta is measurable.

description: Queue a change to one of the core post fields (post_title, post_excerpt, post_name, post_status, post_author). Lands in the Pending Changes inbox in wp-admin. Nothing changes on the live site until the user approves. post_author (v0.68.4) accepts a user ID, login, email, or exact display name and reassigns authorship on approve — the reliable way to purge a departed provider from Rank Math Person/Article schema and the analytics dataLayer, which both read post_author. Pass success_metrics when the change has a measurable SEO target so edit_outcomes can score the result later. Pass dry_run=true to validate without queueing — useful for self-checks before the human commits to a real proposal.

name: draft_create_redirect

source.description: Old URL or path on this site (e.g. "/old-slug/" or "https://eroflufkin.com/old-slug/").

http_code.description: One of: 301 (default permanent), 302 (temporary), 307, 410 (gone, no destination needed), 451.

reasoning.description: Why this redirect exists. Shown to reviewer.

_diag.description: Diagnostic mode. When true, returns the raw Rank Math storage investigation (table existence, sample rows, LIKE-match results, marker hits) WITHOUT queueing a pending. Used to debug dedup mismatches across Rank Math storage formats.

description: Queue a 301 (or other code) redirect via the active SEO plugin's redirect manager. Currently supports Rank Math. Use for duplicate-content resolution (5639 -> 5652), retired URLs, or any source -> destination mapping that should not be a soft-404. Source is the OLD path (or full URL) on this site; destination is where users should land. http_code defaults to 301. Lands in the Pending Changes inbox; on approval the plugin calls Rank Math's Redirection API. Refuses if Rank Math Redirections module is not active. v0.10.0 dedups against existing Rank Math redirects + same-source pendings; pass _diag=true to inspect Rank Math storage state without queueing.

name: draft_delete_redirect

id.description: Numeric Rank Math redirect id to delete.

reasoning.description: Why this redirect is being removed. Shown to reviewer.

description: Queue PERMANENT deletion of a Rank Math redirect by its numeric id. Use to remove a stale, wrong, or looping redirect — the create side cannot fix those and previously every removal was a manual Rank Math step. Get the id from draft_create_redirect's _diag output or from the redirect_already_exists / reverse_loop error payloads. Lands in the Pending Changes inbox; on approval the plugin calls Rank Math DB::delete (which also purges the redirect cache, so the rule stops firing immediately). Refuses if no redirect with that id exists or Rank Math Redirections is not active.

name: draft_untrash_redirect

id.description: Numeric Rank Math redirect id to restore to active.

reasoning.description: Why this redirect is being restored. Shown to reviewer.

description: Queue restoring a TRASHED or inactive Rank Math redirect back to active, by its numeric id. Rank Math soft-deletes redirects (the row lingers with status trashed/inactive and stops firing); this flips it back to active and purges the cache so it works again. Use when an old redirect should be brought back instead of recreated. Lands in the Pending Changes inbox. Refuses if the id is not found, is already active, or Rank Math Redirections is not active.

name: get_working_state
description: Read the saved job record. Treat it as historical context and resume only when it matches the current user request. Preserve explicit constraints; an active status does not authorize switching tasks, publication, or applying stale SEO recipes.

name: update_working_state

active_task.description: One line: the job in progress.

current_plan.description: The very next action a resuming chat should take.

steps.description: Replace the checklist. Prefix done items with [x].

description: v0.42 — update the current-job record so a brand-new chat resumes EXACTLY here. CALL THIS after every meaningful step: when starting a multi-step job (set active_task + steps + current_plan), after queueing/applying changes (add_steps done markers, update current_plan), when the user states a decision or constraint (add_decisions / add_constraints), when something is left half-finished (add_open_loops) or completed (remove_open_loops). Scalar fields replace; list fields replace via <field> or append via add_<field>. Keep entries one terse line each. Promote permanent site rules to update_site_memory_notes(section=rules) as well.

name: gbp_locations

refresh.description: Re-fetch from Google instead of the cached list. Default false.

description: List the Google Business Profile locations connected for this site (title, primary + additional categories, address, phone, website, place id, maps URL). Read-only — does NOT queue a pending change. Use to audit local categories (categories drive map-pack rank) and to get a location id ("locations/123") for gbp_performance. Requires the Business Profile connection in Settings -> Business Profile. Pass refresh=true to re-pull from Google instead of the cached copy.

name: gbp_performance
description: Local-pack KPI totals for one Business Profile location over the trailing N days: calls (CALL_CLICKS), website clicks, direction requests, and map + search impressions (desktop/mobile). Read-only. location is the resource name "locations/123" from gbp_locations. Data lags ~3 days (the window ends 3 days back). Use for board KPIs and to see which locations get discovery vs action.

name: page_quality_gate

post_id.description: Post id to evaluate.

description: Preview the page-quality gate for a post WITHOUT publishing. Returns blocking defects (placeholder / lorem text, duplicate-template cards — these REFUSE a publish_draft at apply time) + warnings (no in-body images, ungrouped flat card lists >10, thin content) + stats (word_count, image_count). Call this AFTER building or revamping a page and BEFORE queueing publish_draft, and when refreshing/optimizing an existing page, to see exactly what to fix to clear the bar. Read-only.

name: win_audit

post_id.description: The page to audit.

query.description: Target search query this page should win. Recommended.

competitor_urls.description: 2-5 top ranking/cited competitor URLs for the query (from your own web search). Omit for an absolute-only audit.

days.description: GSC window for query grounding. Default 28 (7-90).

description: Local heuristic checklist using stored/fetched observations and optional competitor pages. Scores do not establish ranking quality or predict performance. Information gain and factual freshness require source review and are excluded from numeric totals. Use content_research and content_decision for supported content recommendations.

name: page_robustness_audit

post_id.description: The page/post to audit.

strict.description: Deprecated compatibility argument. Findings now come from verified_page_audit; editorial heuristics are not blocking rules.

description: Compatibility audit now powered by the same fresh evidence engine as verified_page_audit. The old uncalibrated score, fixed citation quotas and automatic CTA/length rewrite prescriptions are retired. score and pass are null; report individual findings, observations, capture conditions and unknowns. A blocked fetch is unverified, not a healthy page or a defect.

name: build_page_from_spec

title.description: Post title (also the H1 context). Required.

slug.description: URL slug. Optional. Ignored with target_post_id.

post_type.description: page (default) or post. Ignored with target_post_id.

style_mirror_post_id.description: Required. A well-built page on this site to sample heading/text/card styles from.

target_post_id.description: Optional. Rebuild-in-place: instead of creating a new draft, queue ONE pending change that replaces this existing post's Elementor tree (elementor_full_import path: fresh element ids, pre-apply snapshot). Response includes target_post_id + pending_id + structure.

seo.description: {title, description, focus_keyword} — written via the active SEO plugin (queued as pending changes when target_post_id is used).

sections.description: Ordered section specs. Each: {template: hero|text_image|card_grid|steps|faq|cta_band|form|map, ...fields per template}. Exactly one hero.

dry_run.description: Validate + return structure without creating anything. Default false. Recommended first call.

override_lint.description: Bypass content lint hard-violations. Default false.

override_images.description: Allow a deliberately image-free page. Default false.

description: v0.40 — compose a COMPLETE Elementor page from a typed content spec in ONE call (vs build_service_page which clones an existing pillar). Section templates: hero (eyebrow?, heading=H1, text?, image{url,id?}, overlay_color?, overlay_opacity?, buttons[{text, url?, popup_id?}]), text_image (heading, html|text, image{url,alt REQUIRED}, image_position left|right), card_grid (heading, intro?, columns 2-4, cards[{icon?, title, text, url?, popup_id?, group?, tier?}] — a card url becomes a REAL link on the icon-box; tier:"primary" flips that card to the primary/red token + red border, all other cards deterministically get the secondary/navy token + navy border), steps (heading, intro?, steps[{title,text}] min 2 — numbered process row, visually distinct from card_grid), faq (heading, intro?, items[{q,a}] — renders an AEO-extractable accordion), cta_band (heading, text?, buttons[{text, url?, popup_id?}], background?), form (page_label REQUIRED — used in the email subject; heading?, intro_html? — standard name/phone/email/message form; recipients from option cc_assistant_form_email_standard with admin_email fallback), map (address? — falls back to option cc_assistant_facility_address, errors if neither set; full-bleed Google Maps embed). form and map do NOT count toward the image requirement. THE 2026 BAR IS ENFORCED: at least one image required (hero bg or text_image; override_images for deliberate text-only); >10 cards REQUIRE a group label per card; one H1 (hero) only; full content lint + placeholder + duplicate-card checks run BEFORE creating anything. Styles are SAMPLED from style_mirror_post_id (a well-built page on THIS site — use suggest_best_mirror). Default: creates a draft + ONE publish_draft pending. With target_post_id: REBUILDS that existing post in place — same composition + lints, then ONE elementor_full_import pending replacing its Elementor tree (snapshot-first, human-approved; seo queues against the target too). Use dry_run=true first to validate the spec + see the structure without creating a post. v0.50 POPUPS: any hero/cta_band button or card may pass popup_id (int, from list_popups) instead of url — popup_id WINS over url when both are given and the plugin emits the exact #elementor-action popup-open link server-side; the response attaches a warn-only popup_not_displayed_on_target warning when that popup's display conditions do not cover the target page (check list_popups(covers_post_id) first — a non-covered popup button silently no-ops).

name: find_duplicate_content

post_ids.description: Array of post IDs to compare. Typically gathered from list_posts(search="topic"). Min 2.

threshold.description: Cosine similarity threshold 0.3-0.99. Default 0.7 (catches near-duplicates). 0.85+ catches only obvious duplicates.

description: Find lexical similarity candidates in stored content. Inspect substantive pages and reader tasks before calling them duplicate; use content_decision before consolidation. Cluster size does not authorize merges.

name: gsc_inspect_url

post_id.description: WordPress post ID. Resolves to the post permalink. Use either url or post_id, not both.

force_refresh.description: Bypass the 1h transient cache. Default false.

description: Calls the Google Search Console URL Inspection API to check indexing status for a single page. Returns: verdict (PASS/FAIL/PARTIAL/NEUTRAL), coverage_state ("Submitted and indexed", "Discovered - currently not indexed", "Crawled - currently not indexed", "Duplicate without user-selected canonical", etc.), robots_txt_state, indexing_state (BLOCKED_BY_META_TAG / INDEXING_ALLOWED / etc.), page_fetch_state (SOFT_404 / NOT_FOUND / SERVER_ERROR / etc.), last_crawl_time, crawled_as (DESKTOP / MOBILE), user_canonical vs google_canonical (mismatch = duplicate-content issue), referring_urls (which pages Google found this from), sitemap (which sitemaps it appears in), inspection_link (deep link into Search Console), and a one-line suggested_fix derived from all of the above. Quota: 2,000 calls/day per property — results cached 1h per URL. Pass either url= (full URL) or post_id= (auto-resolves to permalink). Pass force_refresh=true to bypass the 1h cache.

name: propose_emergency_service_schema

post_id.description: Post or page ID this schema attaches to.

name.description: Business name. Defaults to post title if omitted.

url.description: Canonical URL. Defaults to permalink if omitted.

area_served.description: Town/county/region this page serves (e.g. "Burke, TX" or ["Burke, TX", "Hudson, TX"]).

opening_hours.description: Pass "24/7" for always-open. Or pass a custom array via the array form (not yet supported via tool input).

same_as.description: Social / authority profile URLs (Facebook, Instagram, GBP, etc.).

description: Queue an EmergencyService JSON-LD schema for a post or page. Designed for ER / urgent-care / emergency-services landing pages where Local Pack and AI Overviews want structured local-business signals beyond what the SEO plugin's default Article schema provides. On approval, the plugin stores the JSON in postmeta and injects it via wp_head on the front-end. Pass opening_hours="24/7" to expand to the canonical OpeningHoursSpecification. Geo + areaServed are the highest-leverage fields for local SEO; address + telephone improve Knowledge Panel match.

name: draft_update_postmeta

meta_key.description: Meta key. SEO-plugin keys (_yoast_wpseo_*, rank_math_*, _aioseo_*, _seopress_*) are blocked unless force_raw=true.

force_raw.description: Bypass the SEO-key guard. Use only for migration / data fixes; otherwise prefer draft_update_seo_meta.

dry_run.description: When true, return the validation result without queueing a pending row.

description: Queue a change to a single wp_postmeta entry. Use for non-SEO custom fields (alt text, theme settings, etc.). For SEO fields (Yoast / Rank Math / AIOSEO / SEOPress) the endpoint refuses raw key writes — use draft_update_seo_meta instead so the plugin auto-routes to the active SEO plugin. If you really need to write a raw SEO key (rare, e.g. data migration), pass force_raw=true. Pass dry_run=true to validate without queueing. The response may include claim_removal_warnings (warn-only) when the new value drops text that an earlier APPROVED pending change on this post deliberately added/confirmed.

name: draft_trash_post

post_id.description: ID of the page/post to trash.

summary.description: Optional human-facing summary for the inbox. Defaults to "Trash {type} \"{title}\" (ID N)".

description: Queue a pending change that moves a page/post to the Trash, so you can RETIRE an old page (e.g. one being replaced by a rebuild, or an obsolete Spanish twin) through the human-approval inbox instead of asking the operator to delete it by hand in wp-admin. Reversible: it trashes (not permanently deletes), restorable from WP Trash, and a pre-apply snapshot is taken. Plugin-scoped: only allowlisted post types (page/post) can be trashed. In a bulk "Approve all", trash_post applies BEFORE sibling changes so it frees a custom-permalink URL that a newly published page will claim.

name: draft_add_elementor_widget

parent_id.description: Existing container/section/column id to insert into.

widget_type.description: Elementor widgetType, e.g. heading, text-editor, icon-box, icon-list, price-list, button, image.

position.description: Optional 0-based insert index. Omit to append at end.

description: Queue insertion of a NEW Elementor widget into an existing container. Use this instead of an HTML widget when you need to add native heading/text-editor/icon-box/icon-list/price-list/button/image widgets to a page. parent_id must be a section/container/column id (find with get_elementor_widgets — look at widget paths). widget_type is the Elementor widgetType string ("heading", "text-editor", "icon-box", "icon-list", "price-list", "button", "image"). settings is the widget settings object (same shape draft_update_elementor_widget accepts). position is the 0-based insert index into the parent's elements array; omit to append. The endpoint runs the same content-quality lint as draft_update_elementor_widget on text-bearing settings. v0.50 POPUPS: to make a button/icon-box open an Elementor popup, pass link:{popup_id:N} (id from list_popups) instead of hand-building the action URL — the server replaces it with the exact #elementor-action popup-open link, and attaches a warn-only popup_not_displayed_on_target warning when that popup's display conditions do not cover this page (a non-covered popup button silently no-ops — verify with list_popups(covers_post_id) first).

name: draft_remove_elementor_widget
description: Queue removal of an Elementor widget by id. The pending entry shows a preview of what will be deleted so the reviewer can confirm before approving. Removed widgets are stashed for rollback.

name: draft_add_elementor_container

parent_id.description: Parent container id, or "" to insert at page root.

children.description: Optional pre-built children: [{type, widgetType?, settings, children?}].

override_position.description: Bypass the missing-position warning. Use when appending to page bottom is intentional.

override_map_check.description: v0.34 — bypass the map-first gate. Use ONLY when the page has no existing logical sections to split (very rare). Logged to activity log when used.

override_section_continuity.description: v0.34 — bypass the section-continuity check. Use ONLY when you really mean to split an H2 from its body container. Logged to activity log when used.

override_a11y.description: Bypass the contrast warning for proposed children. Use when the dark section background is handled outside the subtree.

override_section_width.description: Bypass the global section-width rule (1100-1300px boxed, 700-900px heading cap). Use when the section is intentionally edge-to-edge (e.g. a hero).

override_lint.description: Bypass hard lint violations (em_dashes / ai_tells / style_guide / wall_of_text / placeholders / address_consistency / hospital_comparison). Use only after the human accepted the failures.

description: Queue insertion of a NEW Elementor container/section/column with optional pre-built children. Use for adding entire new sections to a page (heading + intro + 4-card row, etc.) without resorting to an HTML widget. parent_id may be empty string to insert at the page root. el_type defaults to "container" (Elementor 3.x flexbox) — use "section" for classic sections, "column" for child columns of a section. children is an optional array of pre-built child specs of shape {type: "widget"|"container", widgetType?: "...", settings: {...}, children?: [...]}, so you can pass a complete 3-card row in one call. The endpoint validates parent existence + container type before queueing. v0.34: ROOT-LEVEL inserts (parent_id="") require get_page_map to be called within the last 10 minutes (HTTP 422 map_not_consulted otherwise) AND refuse positions that split a logical section pair (HTTP 422 section_continuity_violation). Override flags exist but are audited.

name: get_page_style_context
description: Read-only page style scanner. Returns the signals you need so a fresh elementor_widget_add / elementor_container_add matches the existing page styling: Elementor Kit global colors and typography, every widgetType currently used on the page (by frequency), distribution of heading levels, every font family and inline hex color used (by frequency), the 3 most common container shapes (flex direction + wrap + content_width), one full icon-box settings sample ready to clone, and the top-level container ids (good insert targets). Call this BEFORE proposing a new section so your new widget reuses the same color tokens, fonts, and container rhythm the page already runs on.

name: draft_add_accordion_item

accordion_widget_id.description: Widget id of the nested-accordion. Find with get_elementor_widgets.

override_dup.description: Bypass the fuzzy-duplicate guard. Use only when the near-match is a deliberate variant.

description: Queue addition of an item (Q + A) to a nested-accordion widget. Solves the prior plugin gap where FAQ items had to be added manually in Elementor admin because nested-accordion items live in settings.items[] (not reachable via draft_update_elementor_widget array_merge). title is the question heading; content_html is the answer body (HTML allowed). Fuzzy-duplicate guard: rejects when an existing item_title normalizes to the same form (>= 80% similar_text), so question rewrites do not stack into the FAQ. Pass override_dup=true to add anyway when the variant is intentional.

name: draft_remove_accordion_item

item_id.description: The _id of the accordion item to remove (from settings.items[].._id).

description: Queue removal of a single item (Q + A) from a nested-accordion widget. Pair with get_post(widget_id=...) to enumerate settings.items[] and pick the _id of the duplicate or stale item you want to drop. Removes BOTH the title from settings.items[] AND the matching answer container from elements[] so the FAQ does not end up with an empty body. Rollback re-inserts the item at its original index.

name: audit_page_design

post_id.description: Post id to audit.

description: v0.31 — runs 13 design + content-quality checks on a post and returns design_score 0-100 + per-check verdicts. (1) WCAG contrast — color resolver now walks hex + rgb()/rgba() + inline <style="color:#xx"> in editor HTML + __globals__ refs resolved through Kit tokens, so source-Kit colors baked into TinyMCE HTML no longer slip past. (2) heading-order no-skip. (3) heading bold (font-weight >= 600). (4) heading-size hierarchy (H1 > H2 > H3 in computed px). (5) hover-state coverage on buttons + linked icon-boxes. (6) alt-text coverage on images. (7) brand-palette compliance (every explicit hex must be in Kit palette). (8) industry vocabulary — flags banned phrases per detected industry (healthcare bans wellness terms like "infusion therapy" / "Myers cocktail" on emergency-clinic pages; legal bans clinical/cosmetic terms; financial bans medical terms; etc.). (9) cross-domain images (image URLs on a sister-site CDN). (10) schema cross-domain (JSON-LD @id pointing to a foreign domain inside an HTML widget). (11) Google Maps address — flags empty / source-site address still hard-coded. (12) empty containers. (13) adjacent section uniqueness (resolved-bg comparison, not just explicit-bg). Verdicts: pass 80+, warn 60-79, fail <60. Run AFTER any build/import; rerun after edits.

name: list_sections

post_id.description: Post id to list root-level Elementor sections for.

description: v0.31 — return one summary row per root-level Elementor container on a post: section id, position, heading text (closest H1/H2 inside), widget inventory (type=>count), background color resolved through Kit globals, content fingerprint (md5 of all text fields, so the AI can spot duplicate-shape sections that still hold source-site content after a cross-site clone), banned_phrase_hits (industry-aware flags), has_foreign_schema, cross_domain_image_count. Use this to pick which section needs replace_section_content. Returns { post_id, industry, home_host, section_count, sections[] }.

name: list_popups

covers_post_id.description: Optional target page/post id. Adds covers_this_post (true/false/null) per popup, computed from its display conditions. ALWAYS pass this when you are about to wire a popup button on a specific page.

description: v0.50 — list every Elementor popup template on this site (read-only). CALL THIS BEFORE WIRING ANY POPUP BUTTON/LINK: Elementor only loads a popup document on pages matching its display conditions, so a popup-open button on a non-covered page silently does NOTHING (this shipped broken in production once). Pass covers_post_id={target page id} and check covers_this_post on the popup you plan to open — true = will fire there, false = will NOT (fix: Elementor > Templates > Popups > edit > Publish Settings > Conditions > add that page or Entire Site), null = conditions contain rules the parser does not understand (verify manually). Each popup returns: id, title, post_status (non-publish popups never fire), modified, edit_url, conditions (raw _elementor_conditions strings like "include/general" / "include/singular/page/10120" / "exclude/..."), site_wide (include/general with no excludes), included_pages (post ids from include/singular conditions), popup_open_url (the ready-made action link). To wire a button to a popup, do NOT hand-build the URL: pass link:{popup_id:N} to draft_add/update_elementor_widget, or popup_id on build_page_from_spec buttons/cards — the plugin emits the exact #elementor-action popup-open URL server-side and warns when conditions do not cover the target page.

name: list_theme_templates
description: v0.51.6 — inventory every Theme Builder template CPT row on the site, ANY status including trash (read-only). Each row: id, title, post_type, status, template_type meta (_elementor_template_type), taxonomy_types (elementor_library_type slugs), conditions (raw _elementor_conditions), has_elementor_data, edit_mode, modified, edit_url. Also returns conditions_cache: the raw Elementor Pro conditions index (option elementor_pro_theme_builder_conditions) that decides AT RUNTIME which template serves which location. Diagnosis rule: a published template renders ONLY if it appears in conditions_cache — present in its own conditions meta but missing from the cache means the cache is stale; run refresh_theme_builder_conditions. Use this whenever a template "does not show" in Theme Builder or does not render on the front end.

name: refresh_theme_builder_conditions

repair_post_id.description: Optional. Template post id to re-stamp before the cache regen.

template_type.description: Required with repair_post_id. One of: error-404, header, footer, single, single-page, single-post, archive, search-results, section, popup.

display_conditions.description: Optional with repair_post_id. Elementor Pro condition strings, e.g. ["include/singular/not_found404"].

description: v0.51.6 — regenerate the Elementor Pro Theme Builder conditions cache and return the resulting cache. Content-neutral maintenance (rebuilds Pro's index of already-published templates), applied IMMEDIATELY without a pending row — it cannot change any content, only which already-approved templates Pro resolves for each location. Use after list_theme_templates shows a published template whose conditions meta is set but which is missing from conditions_cache (typical causes: template trashed/edited outside the plugin, conditions meta written directly). v0.51.7 repair mode: pass repair_post_id + template_type (+ display_conditions) to RE-STAMP a template whose identity Elementor's save hooks reset (type flipped back to "page", conditions deleted) before regenerating — requires the template-editing opt-in.

name: replace_section_content

post_id.description: Required. Post id to mutate.

section_id.description: Optional. Root-level container id from list_sections. Empty string = whole-page batch.

widget_updates.description: Required. Array of { widget_id, settings } objects. settings is a partial Elementor settings object deep-merged onto the existing widget.

reasoning.description: Optional. Human-visible reason shown in the pending inbox.

override_lint.description: Optional. Bypass the content-quality lint (em dashes, AI-tells, style-guide, placeholder/lorem-ipsum, wall-of-text, address-consistency, hospital-comparison) that now runs on this path. Default false. Same gate as container_add / widget_add.

description: v0.31 — queue ONE pending change that updates many widgets inside a single root-level section atomically. Replaces the pattern of 8-15 separate draft_update_elementor_widget calls (each with its own pending row + race-safety check + reviewer click) when localizing a cloned section. Apply behavior is a deep-merge per widget: scalar fields overwrite, array fields merge by key (so { settings: { title: "X", typography_font_weight: "700" } } leaves all other settings intact). If section_id is empty, mutates widgets anywhere on the page (whole-page batch). All widgets must exist before queueing or the call fails with widget_ids_not_in_section. Returns { pending_id, summary, review_url }.

name: list_image_placeholders

post_id.description: Post id to list image placeholders for.

description: v0.30 — after an import_elementor_data call with strip_images=true, the plugin tracks every stripped image in postmeta with the section heading where it lived, the widget id, the original URL, and the alt text. Call this tool to get the operator-facing list: which photos need uploading + where each one goes. Returns { post_id, placeholder_count, placeholders[] }.

name: export_elementor_data

post_id.description: Required. Post id on THIS site to export.

description: v0.29 CROSS-SITE CLONE — returns the FULL raw `_elementor_data` JSON for a post on THIS site, plus its Kit globals (system + custom colors and typography). Call this on the SOURCE site's MCP server to grab a working page (e.g. Irving 137 IV Therapy pillar), then pass the raw_data + kit_globals to `import_elementor_data` on the TARGET site's MCP server. The pair replaces the broken pattern of "build the same layout from scratch via 13 container_add calls" — that loses flex layouts, hover states, responsive properties, and Kit globals. Use this when porting a working page from one site to a sister site. Returns: { raw_data, post_title, section_count, widget_count, max_depth, kit_globals }.

name: import_elementor_data

post_id.description: Required. Target post on THIS site that receives the cloned tree.

raw_data.description: Required. Raw _elementor_data JSON string from export_elementor_data on a sister site.

replacements.description: Map of search=>replace applied to text-bearing fields. Order matters — longer phrases first. Examples: {"IV Therapy in Irving, TX": "Chest Pain Treatment in White Rock, TX", "irvingwellnessclinic.com": "erofwhiterock.com", "Irving Health and Wellness Clinic": "ER of White Rock"}.

regenerate_ids.description: Default true. Assign fresh 8-char hex ids to every cloned element to avoid collision with existing target ids.

strip_images.description: Default false. Clear all image src URLs (image widget, container background_image, image-typed icons) so operator can upload real photos.

map_kit_globals.description: Default true. Keep system color/typography token refs (primary/secondary/text/accent) so target Kit resolves them; strip unresolvable custom-token refs.

source_kit_globals.description: The kit_globals payload from export_elementor_data on the source site. Optional but recommended for accurate mapping.

snapshot_first.description: Default true. Create a pre_elementor_full_import snapshot before applying so a botched import can be rolled back in one click.

reasoning.description: Optional. Human-visible reason shown in the pending inbox.

dry_run.description: If true, return the transform summary without queueing a pending. Useful to preview which replacements / globals would be applied.

sort_replacements_by_length.description: v0.31 default true. Auto-sort replacements longest-key-first so "Irvingwellnessclinic" matches before "Irving" (fixes the "White Rockwellnessclinic" substring-overlap bug).

replace_in_inline_styles.description: v0.31 default true. Also scrub style="color:#xx" / "background-color:#xx" colors embedded in editor HTML via the color_remap. Source-Kit-resolved colors baked into TinyMCE HTML survive widget-setting remaps without this.

color_remap.description: v0.31 — explicit { source-hex: target-hex } rewrites. Applied to widget color settings AND inline editor HTML (when replace_in_inline_styles=true). Hex / rgb / rgba all accepted. Example: { "#003017": "#11468F", "#ffd900": "#DA1212" } to wipe source-site brand colors during cross-site clone.

strip_cross_domain_schema_html.description: v0.31 default true. Drops html/text-editor widgets whose JSON-LD @id / url / sameAs / mainEntityOfPage points to a host other than the target site. Prevents source-site Person/MedicalClinic/FAQPage schemas from carrying over and linking back to the source domain.

description: v0.29 CROSS-SITE CLONE — writes raw `_elementor_data` (typically from a sister site's export_elementor_data) into a target post on THIS site as ONE pending change. One human approval clones an entire page verbatim. Options: replacements (search=>replace map applied to title/editor/text/title_text/description_text/html/content/link.url/item_title/items[].item_title — longer phrases first, str_ireplace), regenerate_ids (default true, assigns fresh 8-char hex ids to every element so cloned widgets do not collide with existing widget ids on target post), strip_images (default false, clears image src URLs so operator uploads real photos), map_kit_globals (default true, keeps system color/typography refs that auto-resolve on target Kit and strips custom-token refs so inline-hex fallback renders), source_kit_globals (the kit_globals payload from export), snapshot_first (default true, creates a pre_elementor_full_import snapshot for rollback), dry_run (preview transform without queueing). Returns: { pending_id, summary, review_url }. v0.50: the raw_data is scanned for Elementor popup-open action links; when a referenced popup's display conditions do not cover the TARGET post the response carries a warn-only popup_not_displayed_on_target warning (the imported button would silently no-op — see list_popups).

name: build_service_page

mirror_post_id.description: Required. Post id of a working pillar to clone (e.g., IV pillar 137).

title.description: Required. post_title for the new draft.

slug.description: Optional. URL slug; derived from title if omitted.

post_type.description: page (default) or post; must be in site allowlist.

replacements.description: Ordered associative map of search => replace. Order matters — longer phrases (e.g., "IV Therapy in Irving, TX") first, shorter ("IV Therapy") last, otherwise the long-form replace cannot match. Applied with str_ireplace (case-insensitive).

skip_widget_ids.description: Optional. Array of node ids from the MIRROR to drop entirely (subtree). Use get_page_style_context(mirror_post_id) to find root container ids.

seo_description.description: Optional. 120-160 chars recommended. Auto-routes to the SEO plugin in use.

focus_keyword.description: Optional. Rank Math focus keyword (or equivalent on other SEO plugins).

dry_run.description: When true, return the structure summary + lint report WITHOUT writing the post or queueing a pending.

override_lint.description: Set true ONLY when human has accepted the hard-lint failures (em_dashes / ai_tells / placeholders / style_guide).

description: v0.19 macro tool — clone a working service-page pillar (the "mirror_post_id") into a NEW draft page with text replacements applied. Replaces the 13-pending manual build that produced misshapen pages. The mirror page's ENTIRE Elementor tree is deep-cloned with fresh ids (container settings preserved byte-for-byte, including flex_direction/flex_wrap/widths that manual mirroring can't copy), text replacements run across editor/title/title_text/description_text/html/content/icon_list[].text/link.url, optional subtrees are dropped via skip_widget_ids (e.g., drop a pricing-menu container if the new service has no real tiers yet), then the page is created as draft + ONE publish_draft pending is queued so the operator approves the whole page in a single click. Use this instead of stacking draft_add_elementor_container calls when building a new service page.

name: suggest_best_mirror

service_keyword.description: Optional. Filter candidates by keyword that must appear in title or slug (e.g., "iv therapy").

target_language.description: Optional. Polylang/WPML language tag (e.g., "en", "es") to constrain results to same-language pillars.

exclude_id.description: Optional. Post id to omit from candidates (e.g., the page being replaced).

limit.description: Optional. Max candidates to return (1-10, default 5).

description: v0.23 — rank existing service pages by clone-readiness so build_service_page gets a pre-vetted mirror_post_id instead of guessing. Walks pages with non-trivial _elementor_data (>8KB), scores each via pre-publish checks (heading depth, alt text, contrast, word count), and returns the top N candidates sorted by pass_rate then word_count desc. Filter by service_keyword (matched against title + slug) and/or target_language (Polylang/WPML) to constrain to same-niche, same-language pillars. Each candidate returns post_id, title, permalink, pass_rate, word_count, mirror_quality, and language. Call BEFORE build_service_page when you are uncertain which pillar to clone from — picking a low-quality mirror propagates its defects to the new page.

name: page_completeness_score

post_id.description: Page to score.

description: v0.19 structural compare — scores a target page (0-100) against a mirror page's widget-type distribution. Returns score, pass/fail at threshold 80, list of missing widget types (with shortfall counts), and a critical_missing flag for high-signal widgets (reviews, google_maps, image, nested-accordion). Use this AFTER build_service_page to confirm the new page reproduces the mirror's structure, BEFORE approving the publish_draft pending. A score < 80 or critical_missing != [] means the build is incomplete and the new page should not publish yet.

name: service_inventory
description: v0.19 — returns the canonical list of services + price tiers actually sold on this site, by walking every page with MedicalProcedure schema and extracting the menu/pricing cards from its Elementor tree. Each pillar reports its tier_count and a `tiers` array of {title, price, duration, description}. Call this BEFORE building a new service page to know what tiers/prices to use (or to confirm a proposed tier doesn't exist on the site, in which case the build should skip the pricing menu). Replaces the failure mode where invented "Single Session / 3-Session / 6-Session" tiers landed on the live Laser Genesis page.

name: reject_pending_change

pending_id.description: Single pending id to reject (use this OR pending_ids).

pending_ids.description: Array of pending ids to bulk-reject (preferred for multi-reject).

note.description: Rejection reason captured on the pending row for audit.

description: v0.19.1 — Reject one or more pending changes by id WITHOUT the operator opening the inbox. Pass `pending_ids` as an array of integers to reject in bulk, or `pending_id` as a single int. Optional `note` is recorded as the rejection reason for audit. Side effects: (a) pending status flips to "rejected"; (b) if the pending is a `publish_draft` whose target post is still a WP draft, that draft post is trashed and its cc_snapshots rows are cleaned up; (c) other change types just flip status — no destructive cleanup. Returns per-id success / failure + trashed_post_id if a draft was trashed.

name: draft_update_elementor_widget

widget_id.description: Elementor widget id (8-char hex, get from get_elementor_widgets).

settings.description: Object of widget settings to merge.

override_lint.description: Set true ONLY if you have shown lint failures to the human and they accepted them.

dry_run.description: When true, return lint + would-be-pending without queueing.

description:
Queue an update to a single Elementor widget on a page. Find the widget id with get_elementor_widgets first. Settings is an object of fields to merge into the widget. Examples: {"title": "New heading"} for a heading widget, {"editor": "

New content

"} for text-editor, {"text": "New label", "link": {"url": "https://example.com"}} for button, or {"link": {"popup_id": 294}} to make the button open Elementor popup 294 (v0.50 — the server replaces popup_id with the exact #elementor-action popup-open URL and attaches a warn-only popup_not_displayed_on_target warning when the popup's display conditions do not cover this page; verify with list_popups(covers_post_id) first, since a non-covered popup button silently no-ops). The endpoint runs the same content-quality lint as draft_update_post_content on text-bearing widget settings (editor, html, content), so paragraphs > 3 sentences, em dashes, AI-tells, and banned phrases are flagged at queue time. Hard violations refuse unless override_lint=true. The response includes a conflicts list when an earlier pending change already targets the same widget, and a claim_removal_warnings list (warn-only) when the edit removes text that an earlier APPROVED pending change on this post deliberately added/confirmed — verify with the operator before approving those.

name: draft_update_post_content

post_id.description: Post ID whose body to replace.

content.description: Full new HTML body. Replaces post_content entirely on approval.

summary.description: One-line description for the inbox (e.g., "Body expansion: add severity staging + risk groups").

reasoning.description: Why this rewrite makes sense. Shown to the reviewer alongside the diff. Reference the brief and the SERP signals you used.

override_lint.description: Set true ONLY if you have already shown the lint failures to the human and they have explicitly accepted them. Default false: hard violations refuse the change.

force_no_outline.description: Bypass the outline-required gate for large rewrites. Use only for migrations / batch fixes; otherwise call propose_rewrite_outline first.

dry_run.description: When true, return lint + would-be-pending without queueing. Use for self-checks before the human commits.

success_metrics.description: Stated intent, used by edit_outcomes to score the change later. Strongly recommended.

target_query.description: GSC query you expect this rewrite to lift.

target_position.description: Target average position after the rewrite settles (e.g., 3.0).

target_ctr.description: Target CTR after the rewrite (0..1). Often only realistic alongside a meta title change.

eval_window_days.description: How long to wait before scoring the change. 7..90, default 28.

hypothesis.description: One-sentence "I believe X will move Y because Z" so the verdict tool can summarise it.

description: Queue a full post_content rewrite for an existing post or page. WORKFLOW: (1) call prepare_rewrite_brief({post_id}) for the dossier + structure + competitor brief + CTR diagnostic + style guide. (2) For any rewrite where the character delta will exceed ~2000 (roughly 300+ words of net change), call propose_rewrite_outline({post_id, outline}) FIRST and wait for the human to approve the outline. The endpoint refuses large body rewrites without an approved outline within the last 7 days (override: force_no_outline=true). Surgical edits like inline-link inserts (delta <2000 chars) skip the outline gate. The endpoint also runs a content-quality lint at queue time: paragraphs over 3 sentences, sentences over 25 words, Flesch-Kincaid grade 11+, em dashes, AI-tell phrases, banned phrases, HTML cruft, jargon density, bulk-add ratio, deletion ratio, and bigram redundancy with kept text. Hard violations (em dashes, AI-tells, banned phrases) refuse the change unless override_lint=true. The proposed HTML lands in the Pending Changes inbox with the lint_report attached. On approval the plugin saves a snapshot + native WordPress revision, then writes the new content. Use draft_update_elementor_widget per-widget for Elementor posts instead. Provide full HTML with no <html>/<body> wrapper, matching WordPress editor output. Cap is 1MB per call.

name: draft_patch_post_content

post_id.description: Post ID whose body to patch.

patches.description: Ordered list of search/replace pairs. Each search must match exactly once in the current post_content. Max 50 per call.

search.description: Substring from current post_content. Must match byte-for-byte and appear exactly once. Include enough surrounding context to disambiguate if the literal phrase repeats.

replace.description: Replacement text. Typically the search string wrapped in an <a> tag, or the search with a small phrase tweak.

reasoning.description: Why this patch makes sense. Shown to the reviewer alongside the diff.

override_lint.description: Set true ONLY if you have shown the lint failures to the human and they have explicitly accepted them.

force_no_outline.description: Bypass the outline-required gate. Surgical patches almost never trigger it; rarely needed.

dry_run.description: When true, applies patches in-memory and returns lint + would-be-pending without queueing.

success_metrics.description: Stated intent, used by edit_outcomes to score the change later.

description: Surgical alternative to draft_update_post_content for inline edits (link inserts, single-word typo fixes, anchor-text tweaks). Takes a list of {search, replace} pairs instead of the full body, so you never re-emit the whole HTML and never normalize CRLF/curly chars/& entities by accident. Each `search` must match EXACTLY ONCE in the current post_content — if it appears 0 times you get 404 (refetch with get_post), if 2+ times you get 422 (add surrounding context to make the match unique). Patches apply sequentially against the running body, so a later patch can target text inserted by an earlier patch. All the normal protections still apply: lint, outline gate, success_metrics, queue. Use this instead of draft_update_post_content whenever the net change is under a few sentences — it eliminates the deletion_ratio false-positive that triggers on full-body rebuilds. For full-body rewrites (>~25% of the post), use draft_update_post_content with propose_rewrite_outline first.

name: list_divi_modules

post_id.description: Post ID of the Divi-built post.

description: v0.51 — module inventory for a DIVI-built post (has_elementor=false and body starts with [et_pb_section]). Parses the shortcode tree server-side and returns a flat indexed list: index, type (et_pb_text / dipl_fancy_text / et_pb_image / …), depth, structural flag, inner_length, text preview, headings found, and typography attrs (text_font/body_font — Divi font shorthand is family|weight|style|…, so text_font="|600|…" means the whole module renders semi-bold). v0.67 also returns attribute VALUES that carry content, on structural modules too: media (background_image on a section, src on an image, background videos), links (button/module URLs), and text_attrs (title/heading/button_text — visible text that lives in the open tag, not inner content). USE THIS FIRST on any Divi post instead of reading the full body with get_post: it is ~10x smaller and gives you stable module indexes for surgical edits via draft_update_divi_modules. NEVER hand-transcribe a full Divi body — that is slow and drops characters. Heading modules (dipl_fancy_text) hold their text in the fancy_text ATTR, not inner content.

name: find_asset_references

url.description: The media URL, e.g. https://example.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/hero.webp. Root-relative also works.

description: v0.67 — find EVERY place in the database that references a media URL: post_content across all post types, postmeta, options and termmeta. Searches all the spellings a URL takes (raw, JSON-escaped https:\/\/, protocol-relative, root-relative, http twin), so it finds URLs inside page-builder JSON and serialized plugin settings that a plain search misses. USE THIS when a plugin stores content outside post_content and no other tool can reach it — popup plugins, sliders, theme options, custom fields. Also use it before deleting or replacing any image, to see what breaks. Returns each location with a context snippet and whether the value is serialized.

name: replace_asset_reference

new_url.description: URL to store instead. Must already be uploaded.

reasoning.description: Why this swap. Shown to the reviewer alongside the location list.

dry_run.description: Return the location list and what would change, without queueing.

allow_missing_target.description: Set true ONLY when new_url is served from somewhere other than this server (CDN, external host). Otherwise a missing file is refused.

description: v0.67 — swap a media URL for another one EVERYWHERE it is stored, queued as a single pending change for human approval. This is how you change an image that lives in a plugin no other tool can edit (popup overlays, slider banners, theme option backgrounds). Serialized values are unserialized, rewritten and re-serialized so length prefixes stay correct — a naive find/replace on a serialized blob silently destroys plugin settings, and this refuses rather than risk it when a value holds a non-stdClass object. Verifies new_url actually exists on disk before queueing. At apply time every row is re-read and skipped if it changed after queueing. Does NOT delete the old file; undo by running the swap in reverse.

name: upload_media

filename.description: Target filename WITH extension, e.g. "insulin-resistance-symptoms.webp". Sanitised via sanitize_file_name. Use the destination post slug as the stem so the library stays greppable.

content_base64.description: Raw file bytes, base64-encoded. No data: URI prefix.

alt.description: Alt text, written to _wp_attachment_image_alt. Describe what the image SHOWS in the context of its section; do not restate the post title (the featured image already owns that).

title.description: Optional media-library title. Defaults to the filename stem.

post_id.description: Optional post to set as post_parent, which files the image under that post in the library. Does NOT set the featured image and does NOT place it in the body.

description: v0.77 — PUT A FILE INTO THE MEDIA LIBRARY. This is the missing half of the media toolchain: every other tool here can only point at images that already exist, so without this an image had to be dragged into wp-admin by hand before anything could reference it. Send the raw bytes base64-encoded; returns the attachment_id and the real URL. Unlike content edits this does NOT queue for approval, and that is deliberate: a freshly uploaded attachment is referenced by nothing and renders nowhere, so it cannot change what a visitor sees. The step that USES it (draft_patch_post_content, draft_update_elementor_widget, featured_image_id) is queued as normal, so the approval gate still sits in front of every visible change. The extension is not trusted — the bytes are probed and must match it. Raster only; SVG is refused because it is markup and can carry script. Ceiling 12 MB decoded, but resize and re-encode to WebP BEFORE sending: WordPress re-encodes anything wider than big_image_size_threshold and the re-encode is routinely larger than the original. If the filename collides WordPress uniquifies it, "renamed" comes back true, and the returned "url" is the one that actually exists — use it verbatim rather than reconstructing it. Every upload is stamped with _cc_assistant_uploaded for traceability.

name: delete_media

ids.description: Attachment IDs to delete. Max 50 per call.

confirm.description: Default false, which is a dry run reporting what would go. Pass true to actually delete. Deletion is permanent.

allow_foreign.description: Default false. Permits deleting attachments this plugin did not upload. Only pass this when a human has confirmed the specific files are disposable.

description: v0.78 — PERMANENTLY delete unreferenced attachments, files included. The counterpart to upload_media, and the only genuinely irreversible tool here: no approval queue can restore deleted bytes, so the guards sit in front of the call instead of behind it. THREE refusals. (1) Not ours: an attachment without the _cc_assistant_uploaded marker is refused, because the library is full of client photography and one transposed digit would destroy it — allow_foreign=true overrides, and should only be passed after a human has confirmed that specific file. (2) Still referenced: checked against the full-size URL, EVERY registered intermediate size, _thumbnail_id (a featured image has no URL in its row at all), numeric ids inside _elementor_data, AND unapproved pending changes (draft-only writing means a graphic can be queued but not yet live, so live tables alone would call it unreferenced) — any hit and the id is blocked with the locations listed. Post REVISIONS are reported but do NOT block, because superseding a graphic is exactly what creates the revision holding its old URL. (3) Not confirmed: without confirm=true nothing is deleted and you get the plan back, so a mistaken call is a dry run. Use it for superseded generated graphics that a re-render orphaned. Max 50 ids per call. Deletions are written to the activity log.

name: media_audit

min_kb.description: Only report images at least this many KB on disk (default 150).

limit.description: Max rows in the heaviest list (default and max 60).

description: v0.67 — heaviest images in the media library, measured on disk rather than from attachment metadata (which goes stale when a file is replaced over FTP). Reports dimensions, mime type, and the -scaled situation: WordPress re-encodes any upload wider than big_image_size_threshold (2560px default) and serves the re-encode, which for an already-compressed file is routinely LARGER than the original — inflated_by_rescale lists exactly those. Use for page-speed work: run this, then find_asset_references on the heavy ones to see which pages they load on.

name: get_divi_module

post_id.description: Post ID of the Divi-built post.

description: v0.51 — fetch ONE Divi module in full fidelity: complete attrs object plus the exact inner HTML. Use after list_divi_modules when you need the full text of a specific module before editing it. Much cheaper than get_post on a 20KB Divi body.

name: draft_update_divi_modules

post_id.description: Post ID of the Divi-built post.

edits.description: Module edits, each targeting a distinct index from the CURRENT list_divi_modules parse. Max 30.

type.description: Expected module type (e.g. et_pb_text). Safety check against stale indexes.

inner_content.description: Replacement inner HTML for the module. Non-structural modules only; no section/row/column shortcodes.

set_attrs.description: Attributes to set on the open tag: {name: value}. Pass null as value to remove an attribute. Encode double quotes inside values as %22 (Divi convention).

reasoning.description: Why this edit makes sense. Shown to the reviewer alongside the diff.

override_lint.description: Set true ONLY if you have shown the lint failures to the human and they have explicitly accepted them.

force_no_outline.description: Bypass the outline-required gate. Module-level edits rarely trigger it.

dry_run.description: When true, splices edits in-memory and returns lint + would-be-pending without queueing.

success_metrics.description: Stated intent, used by edit_outcomes to score the change later.

description: v0.51 — surgical Divi editing: change the inner HTML and/or shortcode attributes of specific modules WITHOUT re-emitting the body. The server splices your edits into the current post_content, verifies the module tree still parses identically (all-or-nothing), and routes the result through the normal lint + outline + Pending Changes queue — draft-only, human approval required, like every other write. Each edit: {index, type (must match — 409 means your inventory is stale, re-run list_divi_modules), inner_content (HTML, non-structural modules only) and/or set_attrs ({name: value, name2: null to remove}; encode quotes inside values as %22)}. Typical uses: rewrite one paragraph module; fix a heading via set_attrs.fancy_text on a dipl_fancy_text; fix sitewide semi-bold body text via set_attrs {"text_font": "|400|||||||"} on each et_pb_text; image alt via set_attrs.alt on et_pb_image. Max 30 edits per call, one pending change per call. This replaces hand-transcribing Divi bodies through draft_update_post_content — use it for ALL Divi module edits.

name: draft_remove_divi_module

post_id.description: Post ID of the Divi-built post or Theme Builder layout (body_layout_id from list_theme_templates).

index.description: Module index from the CURRENT list_divi_modules parse.

type.description: Expected module type at that index (e.g. difl_dual_button). Guard against a stale inventory.

confirm_children.description: Required only when the module contains nested modules; acknowledges that the whole subtree goes.

reasoning.description: Why removing it is safe. Shown to the reviewer alongside the diff.

override_lint.description: Set true ONLY if you have shown the lint failures to the human and they have explicitly accepted them.

dry_run.description: When true, splices the removal in-memory and returns lint + blast radius without queueing. Use this first.

description: v0.70 — remove ONE module from a Divi body (including Theme Builder header/body/footer layouts). draft_update_divi_modules can only rewrite a module and hard-refuses any edit that changes the module count, so a leftover module could previously only be deleted by opening the layout in the Divi builder — the operation that hangs on large Theme Builder layouts. Built for the real case: an EMPTY module someone dropped into a template and never configured, which still drags its plugin's CSS/JS onto every page the template serves. Pass index + type from list_divi_modules (type mismatch returns 409 = stale inventory, re-list). Refuses sections, rows and columns outright — removing a container silently takes every child with it, which is a layout decision for the operator, not a content edit. If the target module has nested modules inside it you get a 409 listing them; pass confirm_children=true to remove the subtree. Verifies the rebuilt body parses to exactly the expected module count with the surviving type sequence intact, all-or-nothing. Draft-only: routed through the normal lint + Pending Changes queue, and because removal is a genuine deletion the deletion_ratio lint is NOT auto-bypassed.

name: audit_post_links

check_external.description: If true, makes HEAD requests to find broken external links.

description: Audits every link on a post: classifies internal/external, applies citation rules (.gov/.edu always allowed, competitor domains blocked, .com only if in authority list), flags weak anchor text. Pass check_external=true to also detect broken links (slower, makes HEAD requests).

name: pre_publish_check
description: Legacy configurable editorial lint for an existing post. Individual word, sentence, snippet, citation, byline and schema thresholds are local preferences, not universal SEO requirements. Run relevant checks and inspect findings alongside current site rules and verified_page_audit. Its verdict does not certify facts, medical review, indexing or ranking; do not rewrite solely to satisfy heuristic thresholds.

name: get_site_memory
description: CRITICAL: call this at the start of every session before proposing changes. Returns the auto-detected stack (SEO plugin, page builder, multilingual, commerce, caching, theme) plus user-maintained notes. The seo.meta_keys map tells you which postmeta keys to use for that site (Yoast vs Rank Math vs AIOSEO use different keys). If you write the wrong keys you create orphan data the user has to manually clean up. Includes memory_consistency: potential outdated durable guidance, a full-notes fingerprint and precedence/context rules. Phrase flags require review; the scan does not inspect local files.

name: update_site_memory_notes

notes.description: Short markdown line. Keep terse: future you only sees the last ~500 chars in session_recap.

section.description: rules | decisions | sessions (default). Rules and Decisions persist; Sessions is append-only timestamped log.

mode.description: append (default) or replace (overwrites the entire blob — use only when consolidating).

acknowledge_open_loops.description: v0.81: a Sessions note is REFUSED (409 open_loops_unacknowledged) while working_state is active with open_loops. Close them first (update_working_state remove_open_loops / status), or pass true to log anyway; the loops are appended to the note so the next chat inherits them explicitly.

description: Per-site memory log, structured into three sections: Rules (permanent: site conventions, do/don'ts that should persist forever), Decisions (architecture choices worth remembering with rationale), Sessions (timestamped append-only log of what you did this session). CALL BEFORE STOPPING the session with a one-line Sessions append summarizing what you did (e.g. "Proposed 8 em-dash fixes on post 3680"). When the user tells you about a permanent rule or convention, append to Rules section instead so it never gets evicted by daily session logs. Default section is sessions; pass section=rules or section=decisions to write elsewhere. The endpoint sanitizes input — control characters, zero-width characters, and accidental tool-call tag fragments (</invoke>, </function_calls>, etc.) are stripped. Identical back-to-back appends are deduped automatically.

name: draft_update_seo_meta

logical_key.description: description, title, focus_keyword, canonical, og_title, og_description

override_lint.description: Set true ONLY if you have shown lint failures to the human and they accepted them.

dry_run.description: When true, return lint + would-be-pending without queueing.

success_metrics.description: Stated intent, used by edit_outcomes to score the change later. Strongly recommended for title/description changes since CTR delta is directly measurable.

description: Smart SEO meta update that auto-routes to the right postmeta key for the detected SEO plugin. Pass a logical_key like "description", "title", "focus_keyword", "canonical", "og_title", "og_description", or "robots" and the plugin maps it to _yoast_wpseo_metadesc / rank_math_description / _aioseo_description / etc. ROBOTS (v0.71.4): pass a plain directive list as the value, e.g. "noindex", "noindex,follow", "noindex,nofollow", or "index" to clear the override and restore the site default. The endpoint converts to whatever the active plugin actually stores (Rank Math: a real ARRAY; Yoast: the string "1"/"2"; SEOPress: "yes" meaning noindex) and skips the prose lint. NEVER set robots via draft_update_postmeta with force_raw: that endpoint types value as a STRING, and WordPress maybe_serialize() double-serializes an already-serialized string, so the SEO plugin reads back a string where it expects an array and silently ignores the override while the apply still reports success. AIOSEO is deliberately unsupported for robots because it keeps that data in custom tables, not postmeta. Use this instead of draft_update_postmeta whenever you are touching SEO fields, so a Rank Math site does not get Yoast keys. When the post_dossier ctr_diagnostics flags underperforming queries, the meta title/description is almost always the lever — propose a meta change here in addition to (or instead of) any body rewrite. The endpoint lints the proposed value at queue time: length window appropriate to the field (title 30-60, description 120-160), em dashes, AI-tells, banned phrases, suspicious characters, and target-query keyword coverage when success_metrics.target_query is set. Hard violations refuse unless override_lint=true.

name: get_style_guide
description: Returns the active style guide for this site. Read it at the start of any content writing or editing task. Falls back to a sensible default if the user has not customized one.

name: draft_create_post

excerpt.description: Manual excerpt for the post. Recommended; without one WP auto-generates a usually-unflattering preview from the body.

post_type.description: Default "page". Must be in the site allowlist. v0.51.5: "elementor_library" is also accepted when the "Allow editing Theme Builder templates" setting is on — pass template_type (and usually display_conditions) with it to compose a Theme Builder template (e.g. a 404 page) through the same draft->approve flow.

template_type.description: REQUIRED when post_type is a Theme Builder CPT. One of: error-404, header, footer, single, single-page, single-post, archive, search-results, section, popup. Stamps _elementor_template_type + the elementor_library_type taxonomy so the template shows correctly in Theme Builder.

display_conditions.description: Elementor Pro display-condition strings written to _elementor_conditions, e.g. ["include/singular/not_found404"] for a 404 template or ["include/general"] site-wide. Dormant while the template is a draft; on approve the plugin regenerates the Elementor Pro conditions cache so the template goes live in its slot. Add the Elementor tree afterwards via import_elementor_data(post_id, raw_data).

categories.description: Categories for the post. Pass an array of category names (strings) or IDs (integers). Names are resolved against existing terms; missing names are auto-created. Only applied when the post type supports the "category" taxonomy (default for post_type=post). Without this, WP assigns "Uncategorized", which is bad SEO.

tags.description: Tags for the post. Array of strings; missing tags are auto-created. Only applied when the post type supports the "post_tag" taxonomy (default for post_type=post).

featured_image_id.description: Attachment ID of an image already uploaded to the WP media library. Sets the featured image (post thumbnail) on the new draft. Posts without a featured image look bare in lists, social shares, and OG cards.

override_lint.description: Set true ONLY if you have shown lint failures to the human and they accepted them.

dry_run.description: When true, validate body + title without inserting a WP draft post or a pending row. Use for self-checks.

success_metrics.description: Stated intent for outcome scoring on the new post.

category_ids.description: Optional array of WordPress category term IDs to attach on insert. The new post is wp_set_post_terms-ed to these categories before the publish_draft pending is queued, so the draft never lands uncategorized. Get valid IDs from the WP REST /wp/v2/categories endpoint.

lang.description: Optional language slug (e.g. "en", "es"). On multilingual sites this assigns the new post to that language taxonomy via the active engine (Polylang supported; WPML and TranslatePress not yet — see multilingual_warnings in the response). Ignored on single-language sites.

polylang_translation_of.description: Optional existing post_id this new draft is a translation of. After insert the apply layer calls pll_save_post_translations() to pair them. On a 2-language site `lang` can be omitted (derived from the source's "other" language). Source post must already have its language set. Translation pairing is logged in `multilingual_warnings` on partial failure rather than aborting the post create.

slug.description: Optional canonical URL slug (post_name). When omitted, WordPress derives the slug from the title — long H1s produce 100+ char slugs that hurt shareability and SEO.
