Pass an explicit short slug (e.g. "infectious-disease-vector-borne-emergencies-near-white-rock-lake") to set it at create time and avoid a follow-up draft_update_post_meta(post_name). Sanitised via sanitize_title.

workflow_id.description: For a new_blog workflow, bind this draft to its current evidence. Requires post_type=post. Call verify_content_workflow with the returned post ID.

description: Create a new draft post or page in WordPress. The draft is created immediately as draft status (visible to admin only) and queued in the Pending Changes inbox for publish approval. The user can preview the draft in wp-admin and click Approve to publish, or Reject to keep as draft. PREREQUISITE: call brief_for_keyword({keyword}) FIRST so the new post answers a real search intent and avoids cannibalising an existing page. ALWAYS pass `categories` (and ideally `tags` + `featured_image_id`) for post_type=post — drafts left without a category default to "Uncategorized", which hurts SEO and shows as a fail in Check up. Pass an explicit `slug` to control the post URL — long H1s otherwise produce 100+ char auto-generated slugs. The endpoint runs the same content-quality lint as draft_update_post_content on the proposed body (em dashes, AI-tells, banned phrases as hard violations; paragraph/sentence length, reading level, HTML cruft, jargon as warnings) and an H1-appropriate lint on the title (em dashes, AI-tells, banned phrases, suspicious chars; NO SERP-length window, since H1 routinely exceeds 60 chars and the Rank Math SEO title is set separately via draft_update_seo_meta). Hard violations refuse unless override_lint=true. On multilingual sites pass `lang` (language slug, e.g. "es") to assign the new post to that language. Pass `polylang_translation_of` (existing post_id) to also pair it as a translation of that source — on a 2-language site `lang` can be omitted and is derived from the source's "other" language; on 3+-language sites pass both. Multilingual issues surface as `multilingual_warnings` in the response without failing the create. For a new_blog content_workflow pass workflow_id and post_type=post, then call verify_content_workflow. If an error reports existing post/pending IDs, inspect those records before retrying.

name: polylang_link_translations

pairs.description: Array of pair objects. Each pair maps language slugs to post IDs covering all translations of one content item.

force_language.description: When true, overwrite a post's existing language if it conflicts with the pair (e.g. an EN post mistakenly tagged as ES). Default false — conflicts return an error on that pair without touching it.

description: Bulk-link Polylang translation pairs in one call. Use this when posts already exist but were never paired (e.g. duplicated via a Duplicate Post plugin, or created before draft_create_post supported `polylang_translation_of`). Each pair is a map of {language_slug: post_id} covering all translations of one content item, e.g. {"en": 4986, "es": 5009}. The endpoint validates that each post is in the claimed language (refuses overwrite unless force_language=true), then writes the Polylang post_translations taxonomy term so the language switcher and hreflang tags work. Returns per-pair {ok, linked} or {ok:false, errors} so partial failure is visible. Polylang only — WPML and TranslatePress are not supported here.

name: create_category

slug.description: URL slug. Optional — defaults to sanitised name.

description.description: Optional category description shown on archive pages.

parent.description: Optional parent category term ID for hierarchy.

description: Create a new WordPress category term IMMEDIATELY (no pending review — categories are organisational metadata, not content). Idempotent: if a term with the same slug (or name when slug omitted) already exists, returns that existing term instead of erroring. Returns the term_id you can then pass to draft_update_categories or as part of category_ids on draft_create_post.

name: list_categories
description: List every WordPress category term on the site with its term_id, name, slug, parent, and post count. Read-only. Useful before queueing draft_update_categories to confirm a target term_id, or before create_category to avoid duplicates.

name: list_product_categories

full.description: Return complete description HTML instead of 240-char excerpts. Default false.

description: v0.53 — list taxonomy terms with their SEO state: term_id, name, slug, parent, product/post count, front-end permalink, archive description (+ word count), and Rank Math term SEO title/description. Defaults to WooCommerce product_cat (the "money pages"); pass taxonomy="category" for blog categories. v0.69: descriptions are returned as 240-char plain-text excerpts by default (a 70-term catalog previously produced a 125KB response); pass full=true when you need complete description HTML. Read-only recon for the category-page optimization loop: description_words=0 means the archive is a bare product grid with no rankable content. Pair with draft_update_term to fix.

name: list_installed_plugins

include_inactive.description: Default true. Set false for active plugins only.

description: v0.65 — enumerate EVERY plugin on the site (active and inactive), not just the curated list site_memory sniffs for. Returns slug, display name, version, active state, text domain, and new_version when an update is pending, plus must-use plugins and drop-ins which get_plugins() hides and which routinely carry site-breaking behaviour. Use this INSTEAD of assuming what is installed: whoami's detected stack only recognises plugins it was explicitly taught (Yoast, Rank Math, Elementor, WooCommerce...), so feed plugins, currency switchers, fraud tools and the like are invisible to it. Pair with stack_admin_menu to find where a plugin's settings screen lives and get_plugin_settings to read what it is set to. Read-only.

name: stack_admin_menu
description: v0.65 — return the REAL wp-admin menu tree: every top-level menu and submenu with its label, page slug, required capability, and the exact admin URL an operator would click. This is what stops the assistant guessing at navigation and telling the operator to look for a tab that does not exist. IMPORTANT, and the reason this is a snapshot rather than a live read: third-party plugins only register their admin_menu callbacks when is_admin() is true (Elementor gates `new Admin()` behind it in includes/plugin.php:727), so a REST request CANNOT rebuild the tree — it would silently omit most plugins while looking complete. The tree is therefore captured during real wp-admin page loads and served here with captured_at and age_hours. If available=false, no admin page has been loaded since the plugin was updated: ask the operator to open any wp-admin screen once. If age_hours is large, treat the tree as possibly stale. Read-only.

name: get_plugin_settings

slug.description: Plugin folder slug from list_installed_plugins (e.g. "woo-multi-currency"), or the active theme's slug (e.g. "divi") to read theme options instead.

description: v0.65 — read a plugin's (or, v0.69, the active THEME's) CURRENT stored settings from the options table, so the assistant can state what a setting is actually set to instead of guessing. Pass the active theme's slug (e.g. "divi") and it resolves against the theme instead: same prefix heuristics plus a source scan of the theme directory (catches Divi's et_divi Theme Options) plus theme_mods_{stylesheet} customizer values — result carries type:"theme". Returns matched option names, their autoload flag, and their values, plus which name prefixes were tried and which options the Settings API registry confirms. SECRETS ARE NEVER RETURNED: any option whose key matches a credential pattern (secret/token/password/api_key/license/auth/private/webhook/signing...) or whose value looks like a credential by shape (Stripe sk_live, JWT, PEM block, long high-entropy token) is replaced with a redaction marker, recursively through nested arrays. The assistant learns the setting EXISTS but never receives it. TWO HONEST LIMITS: (1) WordPress has no formal plugin-to-option mapping, so options are matched by name prefix derived from the slug and text domain — a plugin storing settings under an unrelated key returns zero rows, and absence here is NOT proof it is unconfigured; (2) results are capped for response size. Read-only; this never writes a setting. Follow with inspect_plugin_capability for actual runtime constraints and applicability before planning feature changes.

name: get_kit_settings
description: v0.76 — read the active Elementor kit (Site Settings): the global colour and typography registries with the EXACT dot path each row is written by (system_colors.primary.color, custom_colors.<title>.color), the site-wide levers people come here for (link_normal_color, link_hover_color, link underline, body/heading colours, button and form field colours; null = theme default applies, which on the Hello theme means #cc3366 links), every scalar setting, and the names of nested settings. This is where site-wide WCAG contrast fixes live: one kit change replaces hundreds of per-widget edits. Read-only.

name: draft_update_kit_setting

path.description: Dot path into the kit settings, e.g. "link_normal_color" or "system_colors.primary.color".

value.description: New scalar value (string, number, or boolean).

allow_create.description: Permit creating a scalar key that does not exist yet. Never creates list rows.

dry_run.description: Return the before/after without queueing.

description: v0.76 — CHANGE one leaf of the Elementor kit (Site Settings), draft-queued for approval. Paths come from get_kit_settings; list rows are addressed by _id, title, or index (system_colors.primary.color, custom_colors.Brand Red.color, system_colors.0.color). Colour paths are validated (#RRGGBB, rgba(), hsla(), or an empty string to reset). REFUSES paths that do not exist unless allow_create=true, because a mistyped key is stored and never rendered: the setting would look changed while doing nothing. allow_create is for keys Elementor reads but the site never set (link_normal_color on a site that always used the theme default) and can never invent a new colour row. Rollback restores the entire prior kit blob. On approval the Elementor CSS cache is flushed and the front page is re-read by page_facts; prove a global colour with wcag_sweep or render_probe on a page that uses it. Typical uses: link colour + underline for site-wide contrast (link_normal_color, then link_normal_typography_typography=custom and link_normal_typography_text_decoration=underline), darkening a brand red that sits at 4.4:1 on grey (system_colors.primary.color), body text colour.

name: get_rank_math_schema

post_id.description: Post or page id.

description: v0.65 — read the Rank Math schema attached to a post. Reports which generation the site is on: "schema_builder" (modern, one PHP-serialized array per node in postmeta rank_math_schema_<Type> — a CAPITALISED key nothing else in this plugin can read or write) or "legacy_snippet" (flat lowercase rank_math_snippet_* scalars, which draft_update_postmeta already handles). For each schema_builder row it returns the node @type and a FLATTENED dot-path map of every leaf (e.g. "offers.price", "offers.priceCurrency", "review.reviewRating.ratingValue") plus a list of which leaves hold Rank Math %variable% placeholders resolved at render time. Also returns rank_math_rich_snippet, the legacy master switch: setting it "off" suppresses Rank Math's ENTIRE @graph (Organization, WebSite, BreadcrumbList, Product), not just one node. Run this before draft_update_rank_math_schema to learn the exact dot paths, and after apply alongside render_probe to confirm the rendered JSON-LD changed.

name: draft_update_rank_math_schema

post_id.description: Post or page id.

set.description: Object of dot-path => scalar value. Example: {"offers.price": "38999"}.

meta_key.description: Which row, e.g. rank_math_schema_Product. Optional when the post has exactly one; required when it has several.

reasoning.description: Why this change makes sense. Shown to the reviewer.

dry_run.description: When true, validate and return the would-be change without queueing.

description: v0.65 — queue a field-level merge into one Rank Math Schema Builder row (postmeta rank_math_schema_<Type>). Pass set{} as dot-path => scalar, e.g. {"offers.price":"38999","offers.priceCurrency":"CAD","offers.availability":"InStock"}. ONLY the supplied paths change; every other leaf, including %variable% placeholders like %seo_title%, is carried through byte-identical so it keeps resolving per post. This is the only write path for these rows: draft_update_postmeta runs the key through sanitize_key (which lowercases the Type suffix) and stores a flat string, which would destroy the array. Guards: the parent branch must already exist (add leaves, do not invent structure); price must be bare digits with no currency symbol or thousands comma; priceCurrency must be a 3-letter ISO code; availability must be a real schema.org token; dates must be YYYY-MM-DD; writing a %variable% is refused. Draft-only — nothing changes until the human approves, the pre-merge array is snapshotted for an exact revert, and apply refuses if the row was edited in Rank Math after queueing. One live pending per row (a second supersedes the first), so change several fields in one call. Does NOT create schema: if a post has no rank_math_schema_* row the node must be added in Rank Math's own UI first. Does NOT touch rank_math_rich_snippet.

name: draft_update_plugin_setting

path.description: Dot path to the leaf inside a nested option, e.g. "feedrules.thousand_separator". Omit to replace a scalar option outright.

value.description: New scalar value (string, number, or boolean). Empty string blanks the setting.

allow_create.description: Default false. Creation also requires an explicit registered REST schema for this path; model certainty is not evidence.

dry_run.description: Return the before/after without queueing.

description: Draft one scalar leaf in a stored plugin option. First get_plugin_settings(slug), then dry_run=true, then queue for human approval. Creation requires allow_create=true AND an explicit registered REST schema. Existing storage paths without a schema are labelled storage_path_observed with feature_effect=unknown; existence does not prove accepted choices, licensing or a working feature. Protected core/credential options are refused. Apply rechecks the schema and refuses changed option snapshots, then reads the result back. Rollback refuses to overwrite later changes and checks that restoration succeeded. Verify real plugin output after approval.

name: draft_bulk_assign_term

taxonomy.description: Target taxonomy, e.g. product_brand, product_cat, post_tag.

term_id.description: Term to assign. Must already exist.

source_term.description: For match_type=in_term: term id whose members (incl. sub-terms) to tag.

dry_run.description: Return the plan without queueing.

description: v0.69 — assign ONE taxonomy term (brand, category, tag) to MANY posts in a single approval. Built for the job wp-admin does badly: tagging hundreds of products with their manufacturer. THREE WAYS TO MATCH: match_type="title_contains" (SQL LIKE on post_title ONLY — deliberately narrower than the wp-admin product search, which also matches descriptions and mis-tags accessories that merely mention a brand); match_type="in_term" with source_term=<term id> (that term AND all its sub-terms, which is what the admin category filter fails to do — it misses products sitting in deeper leaves); match_type="post_ids" with an explicit list. Draft-only like every write: returns a PLAN (total_matched / already_had / to_change + a sample of real titles) and queues ONE pending change for human approval. Rollback restores the exact previous terms on every post, including posts that had none. The term must already exist — this never creates terms. Post types: post, page, product. Capped at 600 targets per plan; re-run for the remainder. Pass dry_run=true to see the plan without queueing.

name: draft_update_term

description.description: New archive description HTML. Omit to leave unchanged.

seo_title.description: Rank Math term SEO title. Omit to leave unchanged; empty string deletes.

seo_description.description: Rank Math term SEO description. Omit to leave unchanged; empty string deletes.

reasoning.description: Why this update makes sense. Shown to the reviewer.

dry_run.description: When true, return lint + would-be-pending without queueing.

override_lint.description: Set true ONLY if the human has accepted the lint failures.

description: v0.53 — queue a category (taxonomy term) update through the Pending Changes inbox: the archive description (HTML allowed: h2/h3/p/a/strong/ul/li survive WordPress term-description kses) and/or the Rank Math term SEO title and description. Draft-only like every other write: nothing changes until the human approves; the prior values are snapshotted on the pending row and restored on revert. Description runs the standard content lint (em dashes / AI-tells / banned phrases are hard blocks); seo_title/seo_description run the meta lint with length windows (title 30-60, description 120-160). Two queued updates for the same term auto-supersede (newest wins). Empty string for a seo_* field deletes that term meta. This is the tool for thin WooCommerce category pages: write a real intro (what the category covers, brands stocked, local pickup/delivery) so the archive has rankable content instead of a bare grid.

name: delete_category

term_ids.description: Array of category term IDs to delete. Get IDs from list_categories.

force.description: When true, delete a term even if it has posts attached. Default false. Use only after confirming the posts have been reassigned or that orphaning them is intended.

description: Delete one or more WordPress category terms IMMEDIATELY (no pending review — categories are organisational metadata). Safety gate: refuses any term that still has posts attached (count > 0) unless force=true is passed, and ALWAYS refuses to delete the WP default category as configured in Settings → Writing. Pass an array of term_ids for bulk delete; non-existent ids return ok:false with error:not_found and do not abort the batch. Useful for cleaning up duplicate or legacy categories left behind by translation-plugin migrations.

name: draft_update_categories

category_ids.description: WordPress category term IDs to attach.

append.description: When true, ADD these categories without removing existing ones. Default false (replace).

description: Queue a category-assignment update for an existing post. Replaces the post category set with the provided term IDs (default — same as wp_set_post_terms with append=false). Pass append=true to ADD without removing existing categories. Validates each term ID at queue AND apply time so a stale pending does not silently no-op.

name: review_health

refresh.description: Fetch from Google before reporting instead of reading the daily cache. Default false.

description: Summarizes connected Google Places review data and local review thresholds. The score/thresholds are heuristic, not Google ranking weights. Cached review samples are limited (up to five); recency, pace and response rate cannot be treated as a complete review history. refresh=true requests a refresh; not_configured means a connection is missing.

name: gsc_status
description: Returns Google Search Console connection status: configured (Client ID/Secret saved), connected (OAuth tokens present), selected property, last sync timestamp, last error, cached row count. Call this before any other gsc_* tool. If not connected, ask the user to visit Settings > Search Console in wp-admin.

name: gsc_opportunities

min_position.description: Lower bound for average position. Default 5.

min_impressions.description: Minimum total impressions in the window. Default 50.

days.description: Trailing window in days. Default 28, cap 90.

description: Observed GSC queries in a configurable position/impression window, useful for improving existing visibility. This is one limited opportunity source. Empty results never prevent new niche content; use plan_blog_content for new blogs.

name: gsc_low_ctr
description: Lists pages with high impressions and low click-through rate. Candidates for title and meta description rewrites. Returns rows of {page, impressions, clicks, ctr, position}. Reads from the local cache.

name: gsc_missing_mentions
description: Finds (page, query) pairs where the page already ranks but the query terms do not appear in the page title or body. Strong signal that adding a section, FAQ entry, or paragraph mentioning that query would lift rankings. Returns rows annotated with post_id, post_title, edit_url.

name: gsc_page_queries

post_id.description: WordPress post ID.

page.description: Full page URL as in GSC. Use if post_id is not handy.

description: Returns every query a single page ranks for in the trailing window, sorted by impressions. Use either post_id (preferred, plugin resolves the permalink) or page (full URL as it appears in GSC). Returns {page, days, count, queries: [{query, impressions, clicks, ctr, position}]}.

name: gsc_trends

window_days.description: Window length in days for both halves of the comparison. Default 7, cap 30.

lens.description: all | decay | rise | new_striking | lost. Default all.

description: Week-over-week trend lenses comparing the last N days against the equal-length prior window. lens="all" (default) returns a summary across decay, rise, new_striking, lost. lens="decay" returns pages losing clicks or rankings; "rise" the inverse. lens="new_striking" returns (page, query) pairs that newly entered position 5..15. lens="lost" returns queries that ranked before but stopped ranking. All data from the local cache, no external HTTP.

name: list_recent_edits
description: Lists recently applied changes recorded by the plugin, each annotated with a quick GSC outcome status (pending if too early to measure, otherwise verdict positive/flat/negative based on click delta). Use this as the starting point for "did our last edit work" investigations.

name: get_edit_outcome

edit_id.description: ID of an edit row from list_recent_edits.

description: Detailed before/after analysis for a single recorded edit. Compares 14 days of GSC data ending the day before the edit against up to 14 days starting 3 days after the edit (skipping the GSC reporting lag). Returns per-query position/click/impression deltas (normalized for asymmetric windows), top movers, top decayed queries, and an aggregate verdict. Returns status=pending with a "ready_in_days" countdown if not enough post-edit data exists yet.

name: gsc_anomalies

window_days.description: Recent window in days. Default 7, cap 14.

baseline_days.description: Baseline length in days. Default 28, cap 60.

description: Pages whose recent click count is statistically anomalous vs a 28-day baseline (z-score >= 1.5). Filters out noisy normal variation. direction="decay" for losers, "rise" for risers, "both" for either.

name: gsc_ai_overview
description: Legacy tool name for observed search-appearance data. Non-Web appearances are not confirmed AI Overviews. Inspect the returned measurement type; do not add appearance segments to total Web traffic.

name: aio_ctr_drop_alert

min_impressions.description: Minimum total impressions in window. Default 500.

max_position.description: Only consider pages ranking at or above this position. Default 5.0 (i.e. avg position ≤ 5).

max_ratio.description: Flag if actual_ctr / expected_ctr ≤ this. Default 0.5 (CTR at half of expected or worse). Set 0.7 for a wider net, 0.3 for hard outliers only.

days.description: Trailing window in days. Default 28, cap 90.

description: Low-CTR review candidates compared with a heuristic curve. AI causation and lost-click estimates are not established; inspect measurement, intent, demand and actual result presentation before choosing an edit.

name: gsc_intent_breakdown

post_id.description: Restrict to one page. 0 = site-wide.

description: Groups the queries a page (or all pages) ranks for by search intent: informational, commercial, transactional, navigational, local, branded, other. Returns each bucket with impressions/clicks totals + 5 sample queries. Use for "is this page covering all the intents around its topic" decisions. Pass post_id=0 for site-wide.

name: llm_crawls
description: How many times AI bots (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, Google-Extended, etc.) crawled this site in the last N days. Returns total hits, breakdown by bot, and top crawled paths. Tracking is opt-in: returns enabled=false until the user enables it in Settings > General.

name: links_summary
description: Site-wide internal linking rollup: total edges, orphan count and percentage, top hubs (most-linked-to pages), top emitters (most-linking-out pages). Reads the wp_cc_link_graph table that is rebuilt nightly via cron.

name: links_orphans

include_pending.description: When true, include orphans that already have a queued pending inbound link (annotated with pending_inbound). Default false.

description: Lists published pages that have ZERO inbound internal links. By default, also drops orphans that already have a queued (pending) inbound edit awaiting approval — set include_pending=true to see those rows annotated with `pending_inbound: { count, pending_ids }`. Each orphan is a candidate to either receive a link from a related hub, get merged into one, or be removed.

name: links_audit_post

post_id.description: WordPress post ID.

description: Full internal linking audit for a single post: existing inbound + outbound links, plus deterministic suggestions for new links to add (other posts whose title appears unlinked in this body) and for new inbound links to acquire (pages whose body mentions this post's title without linking). All proposals are exact phrase matches — Claude can refine them with context.

name: links_rebuild
description: Force a rebuild of the internal link graph (normally rebuilt nightly). Returns immediately and queues the rebuild via cron so the request never blocks. Run after a large content migration.

name: content_audits

limit.description: Max posts to scan. Default 200, cap 1000.

description: Scans published content for three quality issues: (1) cross-site brand references that signal a template was pasted from a sister site, (2) AI-generation artifacts in slugs (humanizer / select-N-more-words / etc.), (3) legacy "Related guides" appendix sections (current preference is inline links only). Returns a flat issue list with codes the operator can resolve through the normal Pending Changes flow.

name: connection_test
description: Verifies the MCP <-> WordPress connection is healthy: confirms the app password works, the site identity service is responding, and reports whether the host PHP has the curl/openssl extensions loaded (needed for outbound HTTPS from the bundled Local CLI). Useful first step when debugging .mcp.json setup.

name: topical_authority

limit.description: Max posts to scan. Default 200, cap 1000.

days.description: GSC window in days. Default 28, cap 90.

description: Read topical relatedness clusters with observed GSC and link metrics. Cluster size, similarity and low impressions do not justify merging or removal. content_gaps are only GSC query candidates; an empty list is not no opportunity. For new blogs, use plan_blog_content to explore niche source pages and reader questions.

name: list_topic_clusters
description: Returns persistent topic clusters defined for this site (pillar + supporting page groupings, human-approved). Different from topical_authority which clusters on-the-fly via math — these are human-curated groupings persisted in the DB. Call this near the start of any session that involves SEO or content work. Once clusters exist, you should read just one cluster's pages instead of every page on the site. Returns each cluster's id, slug, name, description, pillar_post_id, and member_count.

name: get_topic_cluster
description: Returns one cluster's full details: cluster metadata + every member page (post_id, title, role, edit_url). Use this when working on a topic — read only the relevant cluster's pages instead of list_posts across the whole site.

name: propose_topic_cluster

pillar_post_id.description: Post ID of the pillar (canonical) page for this topic.

reasoning.description: Why this grouping. Shown to the human reviewer.

success_metrics.description: Stated intent for outcome scoring on the cluster (e.g. expected pillar query lift after consolidation).

dry_run.description: When true, return the would-be-cluster preview without queueing.

description: Queue a new topic cluster as a Pending Change for human approval. Provide name, optional description, optional pillar_post_id, and an array of supporting_post_ids. The user reviews the proposal in wp-admin and approves to commit it. Use after reading the site's pages and identifying a coherent topic group.

name: propose_cluster_assignment

dry_run.description: When true, return the would-be-assignment preview without queueing.

description: Queue an assignment of a single page into an existing cluster as a Pending Change for human approval. Use when you encounter an unclustered page that fits an existing cluster, or when you want to move a page between clusters.

name: bulk_propose_cluster_assignments

dry_run.description: When true (default), returns candidate matches without queueing anything. Set false to actually queue propose_cluster_assignment for each match meeting the threshold.

min_score.description: Token-containment threshold 0..1. Default 0.4 (40% of post tokens must appear in cluster signature). Lower for more aggressive matching, higher for stricter.

limit.description: Max unclustered posts to evaluate. Default 200.

max_queue.description: Max pending changes to queue in one call. Default 20 — keeps the inbox reviewable.

description: v0.21.0 — auto-suggest cluster assignments for every unclustered post on the site in one batch. Scores each unclustered post against every existing cluster using token containment (what fraction of the post's title + excerpt tokens appear in the cluster's signature: name + description + member titles). For each post, picks the highest-scoring cluster; if score >= min_score, queues a propose_cluster_assignment pending change. Defaults to dry_run=true so a first call NEVER queues — review the candidates list, tune min_score if needed, then re-run with dry_run=false. Use this to clear an "84 unclustered pages" backlog without triaging one-by-one. Reviewer still approves each queued assignment in the Pending Changes inbox.

name: gsc_cannibalization

min_impressions.description: Minimum impressions per page to count. Default 25.

max_position.description: Pages must rank within this position to count as competing. Default 30.

description: Find query/page overlap candidates over a reporting window with weighted position. This does not prove simultaneous competition, diluted rankings or lost traffic. Inspect reader tasks, language and outcomes through content_decision before proposing changes.

name: audit_post_images
description: Audits every in a post for SEO + accessibility issues: missing alt, empty alt, alt too short or too long, alt that looks like a filename, src filename that is a hash or generic name. Reads both classic post_content and Elementor widget editor fields. Pair with draft_update_postmeta or draft_update_elementor_widget to queue alt-text fixes.

name: refresh_queue

min_click_drop.description: Minimum click decline to include. Default 5.

min_age_days.description: Skip pages modified in the last N days. Default 90.

description: Returns a prioritised list of pages worth refreshing. Combines GSC click decline (last 7 days vs prior week) with post age (post_modified) into a priority_score. Filters by min_click_drop and min_age_days so trivial fluctuations and recently-updated posts are excluded. Use as a content-strategy starting point: "what should I work on this week?".

name: click_depth_audit

max_depth_warn.description: Depth at which pages are flagged as buried. Default 4.

buried_only.description: If true, only return buried pages.

description: Computes how many clicks each page is from the homepage (BFS over the internal link graph). Returns a depth histogram and a list of pages with their depth — pages at depth >= max_depth_warn (or unreachable) are flagged buried. Buried pages get less crawler attention from Google. Use to find pages that should get more inbound internal links from higher-traffic pages.

name: post_dossier
description: One-call deep dive on a single post: title/word_count/last_modified, cluster memberships (and role in each), full pending+history of changes, internal inbound and outbound links with anchor text, and top GSC queries (last 28 days). Use this instead of calling get_post + list_pending_changes + clusters_for_post separately when working on one page.

name: analyze_post_structure
description: Returns the structural fingerprint of a post for search-intent matching: word_count, intro_word_count, h2 count + how many are questions, FAQ shape, list count, table count, step shape, CTA count, schema presence, per-section word counts, and an intent_fingerprint label list (how-to / faq / listicle / comparison / definitional / commercial). Pair with WebFetch on the SERP top 3 to compare your structure to what is actually winning.

name: competitor_brief
description: Returns a brief about a target keyword: the user's configured competitor_domains list, our own pages already ranking for the keyword (with impressions/clicks/avg_position from GSC), and a next-step hint. Pair with WebFetch to pull top-ranking competitor pages and identify topics, schema, and structural patterns we are missing. If competitor_domains is empty, the response tells the user to configure them in Settings.

name: weekly_priorities

force.description: Bypass cache and recompute. Default false.

description: Optional maintenance candidate queue from observed metrics. It does not limit requested new content. Use plan_blog_content for niche-based blog growth independently of whether this queue or GSC gaps is empty.

name: brief_for_keyword

keyword.description: Target search query for the new post.

intent_hint.description: Optional override: informational | commercial | transactional | navigational | local.

description: Brief for a proposed query: observed GSC sample, tentative cluster fit and content context. Missing GSC does not mean no demand or a clean slate. Use plan_blog_content first for a new-blog request, including topics with no ranking history. Existing query overlap is not proof of SEO harm; no fixed word count is required.

name: prepare_rewrite_brief

post_id.description: Post ID being rewritten.

keyword.description: Optional. Override the primary keyword (defaults to the highest-impression GSC query for the post).

description: MANDATORY PRE-FLIGHT for any body rewrite of an EXISTING post. One call returns: post_dossier, analyze_post_structure, brief_for_keyword on the top GSC query, competitor_brief, cannibalization filtered to this post, accessibility audit, image audit, the active style guide (raw markdown + parsed banned-phrase list), recent pending/approved edits on the post, a CTR-vs-position diagnostic that flags meta-tag problems vs body problems, and an 11-point rewrite checklist. Always call this BEFORE draft_update_post_content. The plugin server will lint your proposed body at queue time against the same rules surfaced here, so skipping this step just means hard-violation refusals on submit. Pass keyword to override the auto-picked top GSC query; otherwise omit it.

name: propose_rewrite_outline

post_id.description: Post ID being rewritten.

action.description: One of: keep, cut, merge, add, rewrite. Keep = leave as-is. Cut = delete the section. Merge = fold into another section. Add = brand-new H2. Rewrite = same heading, new content.

h2.description: The H2 heading text (existing or proposed).

notes.description: Optional one-line note explaining the action (e.g. "fold into Treatment Paths").

outline.description: Ordered list of outline rows representing the proposed H2 structure of the rewritten post.

rationale.description: One-sentence editorial summary: what the rewrite is changing and why.

summary.description: Optional one-line description for the inbox. Auto-generated from the action counts if omitted.

reasoning.description: Why this plan. Shown to the reviewer alongside the outline.

description: MANDATORY FIRST STEP for any large body rewrite (>2000 character delta). Queue a structured editorial outline as a Pending Change for the human to approve BEFORE you write any HTML. The reviewer sees each H2 with its action chip (keep / cut / merge / add / rewrite) and your notes, signs off on the plan, and only then does draft_update_post_content accept the body. The endpoint refuses big rewrites without an approved outline within the last 7 days (override: force_no_outline=true for migrations). The outline shape is an array of {action, h2, notes} rows plus a one-line rationale.

name: verify_change

pending_id.description: The pending_id returned by a draft_* or propose_* tool.

description: Self-audit a queued pending change. Call AFTER any draft_* / propose_* tool returns a pending_id, so you can confirm the lint passed, the structure delta is what you intended, no sibling pending rows duplicate this work, and success_metrics are set. Returns: pending row metadata, the lint_report attached at queue time, structure_diff (before vs after analyze_post_structure for post_content rewrites — word_count_delta, h2_delta, h3_delta), success_metrics, sibling pending or approved changes on the same post (so you spot stacked work), and a one-line verdict the model can quote. Use this as your post-action check instead of trusting that the queue endpoint return value made it through context.

name: cluster_gsc

days.description: GSC window in days. Default 28, range 7..90.

description: Cluster-aware GSC overlay. Aggregates Search Console data across every member URL in a topic cluster and returns: totals (impressions/clicks/avg_position/queries), top 25 cluster queries with the leading page per query, "pillar misses" (queries where supporting pages outrank or replace the pillar — strong refresh signal), internal cannibalization (queries where 2+ cluster members compete in the same SERP window), and a per-member breakdown of impressions/clicks/avg_position. Use to spot whether the pillar is doing its job and which queries to consolidate.

name: accessibility_audit
description: v0.76 — content-level WCAG audit on the RENDERED page (render probe, cache-busted, document order). Reports empty/unnamed links (img alt and aria-label credited, as a screen reader would), weak link text, heading skips and empty headings in true document order, missing or multiple H1, html lang, skip link presence and a dangling skip target, tables without th, content hidden by aria-hidden, images with no alt attribute (alt="" counts as decorative), role=img without a name, iframes without title, form controls with no label (placeholder is not a label), buttons without a name, autoplay carousels and videos. Every finding carries the WCAG criterion. Before v0.76 this read stale post_content and reported failures the live page did not have; it now refuses to fall back to that. NOT measured here: colour contrast, visible focus, keyboard operability, motion - run wcag_sweep for those.

name: canonical_audit
description: P0 guard. Fetches the rendered HTML of the post permalink and validates rel="canonical" against Google's documented rules: must be in <head>, single tag, absolute https URL, no #fragment, present in source HTML (no JS-injection-only). Returns issues[] with severity (high/medium/info), the resolved canonical URL, and a verdict (pass/warn/fail). Run this BEFORE proposing a meta or slug change — a broken canonical can cause deindex. Codes: canonical_missing, canonical_in_body, canonical_duplicate, canonical_not_absolute, canonical_has_fragment, canonical_cross_referenced (info-only, may be intentional).

name: hreflang_audit

id.description: Post ID. Audits the full translation cluster this post belongs to.

description: P0 guard for bilingual / multi-locale sites (Polylang or WPML). Fetches the rendered HTML of every translation cluster member for this post and validates Google's hreflang rules: reciprocity (every member links to every other), self-reference, absolute URLs, <head>-placement, valid ISO 639-1 + ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes (use "GB" not "UK", reject region-only codes), canonical-cluster agreement (each canonical must point inside the cluster). Monolingual sites or untranslated posts return a clean pass. Codes: hreflang_in_body, hreflang_not_absolute, hreflang_invalid_iso, hreflang_no_self_reference, hreflang_reciprocity_missing, canonical_outside_hreflang_cluster.

name: eeat_coverage_audit
description: Legacy heuristic check of observed byline, schema and citation proxies. Its pass/fail and density thresholds are plugin-defined, not Google requirements or proof of expertise, truth or ranking impact. Inspect actual claims and editorial responsibility. Never invent credentials, provider consent, bylines or Person markup to satisfy it; use verified_page_audit and appropriate subject review.

name: schema_parity_check
description: P0 guard. Validates that every text property of every JSON-LD entity on the page (name, description, headline, performer.name, areaServed, hasCredential, etc.) is visible in the rendered DOM. Google's structured-data policy explicitly forbids marking up hidden content — violation can trigger a manual action. Tokenizes each schema value into 3-word slices, normalized lowercase, and confirms at least one slice appears in the visible body. URLs / pure dates / short tokens are excluded to avoid false positives. Returns issues[] with property + entity @type + the offending snippet. Code: schema_not_in_dom.

name: self_review_detection
description: P0 guard. Detects aggregateRating or Review nodes whose itemReviewed is the site's OWN Organization / LocalBusiness / MedicalClinic / Hospital / etc. Google explicitly forbids self-reviews — the page becomes ineligible for review rich results AND may trip a manual action. Heuristics: match site home host on @id/url, match site title on name, or aggregateRating sitting as a direct property on a self-business node. Clinic sites are a high-risk profile because review widgets often embed schema. Returns findings[] with kind (Review/AggregateRating) + entity_type + match reason. Code: self_review_detected.

name: helpful_content_score

refresh.description: Bypass cache and recompute. Default false.

description: Heuristic content review using local proxies such as text length, headings, citations and byline markup. The 0-100 score and bands are plugin-defined; they do not measure Google helpfulness, truth, E-E-A-T or a confirmed search penalty. Cached in post metadata; refresh=true recomputes it. Use as review prompts alongside subject-matter review and verified_page_audit, never as automatic authority to rewrite or remove content.

name: site_quality_score

refresh_stale.description: Re-score posts whose cached score is older than freshness_days. Caps at rescore_cap to keep one call cheap. Default false.

freshness_days.description: Cache freshness in days. Older entries are stale. Default 14, cap 90.

bottom_n.description: Number of worst-scoring posts to enrich and return. Default 10, cap 100.

rescore_cap.description: Max posts to re-score in one call when refresh_stale=true. Default 10, cap 50.

description: Aggregate of cached local helpful_content_score proxies. Scores and thresholds are plugin-defined review aids, not a Google site-wide score or proof some pages damage the domain. Unscored and stale pages limit coverage. Inspect evidence before recommending edits, deletion or noindex.

name: external_originality_check

keyword.description: Target keyword. Defaults to the post's top-impression GSC query, then to the post title.

description: Read builder-aware source content and evidence coverage for an originality investigation. The response is explicitly not compared. Use content_research with actual competitor URLs; no similarity threshold or statistics quota certifies originality.

name: keyword_research
description: Optional GSC query sample around a seed, plus existing post candidates. This only describes observed site queries. No rows or near misses does not mean no opportunities. Use plan_blog_content to explore source-backed service/niche topics and reader needs beyond GSC.

name: generate_schema
description: Generate Schema.org JSON-LD for a post. Produces an Article (or HowToArticle for how-to intent) for posts, a WebPage node for pages, plus FAQPage when Q/A pairs exist (parses both classic content and Elementor widgets including FAQ accordions). A BreadcrumbList is included only when the active SEO plugin (Yoast / Rank Math) does not already emit one site-wide. Returns the JSON; does NOT write to the live site.

name: propose_schema

reasoning.description: Why this schema. Shown to reviewer.

include_breadcrumb.description: Default false. Force a BreadcrumbList node even when the active SEO plugin (Yoast / Rank Math) already emits one site-wide.

success_metrics.description: Stated intent (e.g. expect FAQ rich result for target_query).

dry_run.description: When true, generate + lint the schema preview without queueing.

description: Generate Schema.org JSON-LD for a post and queue a pending change that writes it to postmeta. Reviewer sees the JSON in the inbox before approval. Use this when the existing SEO plugin is not producing the right schema for the post type. dry_run=true is honored: it generates + lints and returns the would-be schema WITHOUT queueing a pending row. BreadcrumbList is omitted from the @graph when the active SEO plugin (Yoast / Rank Math) already emits one site-wide — pass include_breadcrumb=true to force it. The endpoint validates FAQ items in the proposal against the actual post body — every Question.name must appear in the body and every acceptedAnswer.text must match content visible on the page. Schema for content not visible on the page is rich-results spam and the endpoint refuses it. Also adds an advisory when FAQPage is being added on a site whose SEO plugin already injects schema, so you can run a Google Rich Results Test for duplicate-FAQ.

name: gsc_warehouse_sync

max_dates.description: Date budget for this call. Default 30, cap 120 (each date = 1+ HTTP round trips).

refresh_days.description: Trailing dates always re-pulled to catch late-arriving GSC data. Default 7, cap 30.

backfill.description: Walk backward filling missing history toward the 16-month floor. Default true.

description: Archive retrieved GSC observations in local SQLite without server-side pruning. Upstream API limits, anonymized queries and missing dates still constrain completeness. Refresh recent dates, fill gaps and backfill within available retention. Read coverage before interpreting trends.

name: gsc_warehouse_query

sql.description: One SELECT or WITH statement. No writes — the connection is opened read-only.

description: Run a read-only SELECT (or WITH) against the local SQLite GSC warehouse — instant, no REST round trip, no WAF, full query-level granularity. Schema: gsc_daily(date TEXT 'YYYY-MM-DD', page TEXT, query TEXT, clicks INT, impressions INT, position REAL) with indexes on (page, date) and (query, date); sync_log(date, rows, fetched_at) shows coverage. Positional ? params supported. Examples: striking-distance = SELECT query, SUM(impressions) imp, SUM(clicks) ck, AVG(position) pos FROM gsc_daily WHERE date >= ? GROUP BY query HAVING pos BETWEEN 8 AND 20 ORDER BY imp DESC; page trend = SELECT date, SUM(clicks) FROM gsc_daily WHERE page = ? GROUP BY date ORDER BY date. Results capped at max_rows (default 200) with a truncated flag — aggregate in SQL rather than pulling raw rows. Data is only as fresh as the last gsc_warehouse_sync (check gsc_warehouse_status).

name: outcome_report

window.description: Days each side of the apply date. Default 28, range 7-56.

limit.description: How many recent applied edits to evaluate. Default 20, max 100.

min_pre_clicks.description: Below this many clicks in BOTH windows the verdict is low_data. Default 20.

description: Observational comparison around applied edits using symmetric time windows and a site comparison. Reports clicks/leads, overlapping edits and data readiness. Difference-in-differences estimates do not establish causality without appropriate assumptions and controls; diagnose confounders before reverting an edit.

name: verified_page_audit
description: Use FIRST for page/SEO assessments and before editing a published page. Always fetches new HTML and evaluates fixed versioned rules with pass/fail/review/unknown/not_applicable findings, exact evidence, UTC capture time and fingerprints. Explains differences from the previous audit. CAPTCHA, HTTP failures and cache hits cannot produce a current all-clear. Scope is server HTML only: JavaScript, appearance, Google indexing, rankings and field Core Web Vitals remain unknown. Cite rule IDs and evidence; preserve unknown/review statuses; never turn this into an overall SEO score or claim every aspect is correct.

name: page_facts

post_id.description: Post ID.

refresh.description: Force a fresh capture even if the record is not stale.

description: Server HTML observations for one published page. Refresh defaults to true. Use verified_page_audit for consistent verdicts. refresh=false permits a stored record (up to seven days); never use it as current evidence. Check captured_at, stale, refresh_error, cache_state and collection scope before making claims. Link/image/heading lists are bounded; absence from a truncated list proves nothing. Empty image alt can be intentional for decoration. This does not execute JavaScript or prove what Google indexed. Verification is tied to one apply capture and invalidated by later captures.

name: keyword_targets

owner_page.description: Full URL of the page that should own this query (set).

target_position.description: Position at or above which the target counts as won. Default 3.

notes.description: Optional operator note (why this query matters, competitor names, constraints).

days.description: Measurement window for report. Default 28, range 7-90.

description: Track an operator-nominated target page and observed query position across windows. Owner is an editorial nomination, not a verified Google preference. Low CTR is review only, AI attribution remains unknown, and zero observations do not prove no demand. Use content_decision before changing related pages and plan_blog_content for niche expansion.

name: wcag_sweep

action.description: run (default) | report (summarise the stored last run, no browser).

urls.description: Explicit URLs to audit instead of the sitemap.

max_pages.description: Sitemap cap, default 40 (homepage first, then alphabetical so slices are stable). 1-1000.

keyboard.description: Run the keyboard/focus/form/popup checks (default true; adds ~6s a page).

description: v0.76 — WCAG 2.1 A/AA sweep in a REAL browser, run from the operator machine: Playwright + axe-core over the site sitemap URLs (or an explicit list), every page scrolled top to bottom BEFORE measuring so lazy-loaded backgrounds and gradients do not fake contrast failures (measured: 61 false flip-box failures on one site without the scroll). Adds the checks a static audit cannot do: visible keyboard focus on the first 30 tab stops, skip-link presence and target, whether each form exposes an error to assistive tech when submitted empty (aria-invalid / role=alert / aria-live), and whether an open popup holds focus and closes on Escape. Output: rules ranked critical to minor with WCAG tags, page and node counts and three examples each; rules that are Elementor vendor markup are labelled vendor (report only, do not patch content); contrast_groups collapses hundreds of contrast nodes into the few element+colour pairs behind them (template or kit fixes, queueable with draft_update_kit_setting or Theme Builder widget edits when template editing is enabled); keyboard findings. Results are stored locally; action=report re-reads the last run without a browser. Needs Node.js on this machine; first run installs Playwright and Chromium into ~/.cc-assistant/wcag (one time, a few minutes). Default max_pages=40 keeps a run under ~5 minutes; raise it for a full site (about 8 seconds a page).

name: site_status

days.description: Window length in days, compared against the equal window before it. Default 28, range 7-90.

max_findings.description: Cap on returned "lacking" findings, severity-ranked. Default 8, range 3-20.

description: Warehouse observations and diagnostic hypotheses. Low CTR and long query wording do not establish AI absorption/citation. Multiple URLs are overlap candidates, not proof of harm. Do not reject new niche blogs because GSC gaps are empty; use plan_blog_content. Use content_decision before consolidation or retirement.

name: commodity_audit

limit.description: Top pages by impressions to classify. Default 25, max 50.

description: Classify observed pages as OBSERVE, REVIEW_CTR or REVIEW_DATA. Low CTR is a hypothesis to diagnose; AI absorption and investment/removal decisions are not established by the curve or volume. No automatic STOP or CITE_PLAY recommendations.

name: aeo_snapshot
description: Store a dated snapshot of low-CTR query candidates, crawler requests and separate search-appearance observations. Neither low CTR nor crawler hits certify AI consumption or citation. Legacy snapshots are labeled; only compatible measurement versions are compared.

name: propose_revert

edit_id.description: The applied edit to revert (from outcome_report or list_recent_edits).

force.description: Queue even though newer applied edits on the same post would also be undone. Default false.

reasoning.description: Why — cite the outcome verdict and did_delta_pct.

description: Close the loop on a bad outcome: queue a REVERT of an applied edit as a normal pending change (draft-only doctrine — the human approves the revert like any other change). Finds the snapshot captured just before that edit was applied and queues its restore; the restore itself takes a pre-restore snapshot, so even an approved revert is reversible. Refuses with 409 newer_edits_exist when later edits were applied to the same post (a restore would undo those too) — review them, then pass force=true only if undoing them is intended. Typical flow: outcome_report says verdict=regressed with did_delta_pct well below -10 → check the page yourself (render_probe) → propose_revert(edit_id) with reasoning citing the outcome numbers. Use the edit_id from outcome_report / list_recent_edits.

name: lead_events
description: Daily lead counts from Elementor Pro form submissions — the MONEY metric behind clicks. One aggregate row per (date, post_id, form_name); counts only, nothing personal stored. Compact columns/rows format. Empty rows on a site with no submissions (or before v0.58) is a legitimate "no leads recorded", not an error. outcome_report automatically folds these into each judged edit as leads {pre, post} when data exists — call this directly only for standalone lead analysis (e.g. which pages convert, form performance over time).

name: operator_kit
description: Disaster-recovery + new-machine bootstrap: the SITE stores the operator knowledge, so a fresh laptop (or a fresh Claude with no local skills/memory) can rebuild the working environment from the site alone. Returns: the stored design skills (global visual system + per-site brand — write them to ~/.claude/skills/ as instructed), a ready CLAUDE.md template with this site's MCP server name filled in, a .mcp.json server entry template (only the Application Password needs filling), and ordered new_machine_steps. If whoami works but you have no design skills or site context on this machine, call THIS before doing any design work. Keep the stored skills current with operator_kit_push_skills after editing the local skill files.

name: operator_kit_push_skills

global.description: Full text of the global design-system skill.

site.description: Full text of this site's brand/design skill.

description: Push the CURRENT local design skill file contents to the site's operator-kit storage (option, direct save — operator config, not content, so no pending queue). Pass global (design-system-global SKILL.md text) and/or site (per-site brand SKILL.md text), each max 200KB. Do this after any meaningful skill-file edit so a lost laptop never loses the design system — the site is the backup.

name: operator_brain_status
description: Operator Brain (v0.79): compare THIS machine's operator knowledge (every ~/.claude memory file for this project, every skill, CLAUDE.md, a secrets-stripped .mcp.json template) against the copy stored on this site, file by file. Returns status in_sync | local_missing | local_newer | site_newer | site_empty | both_empty with the exact action, a diff (only_local / only_site / differ with sample paths), and bridge.status telling whether the bin/ files this chat is running match the ones the site ships. whoami already embeds the same verdict; call this for the file-level detail before deciding to push or pull.

name: operator_brain_push
description: Upload this machine's operator brain to THIS site so any other laptop can restore it. Sends only files that are new or changed (index diff) and removes files this laptop no longer has, in chunks; verifies by fingerprint afterwards and reports diverged_after_push instead of assuming success. Direct save (operator config, not content: no pending queue). Run after editing memory or skills. For all sites at once use: php bin/brain-sync.php push

name: operator_brain_pull
description: Restore operator knowledge from this site onto THIS machine. what: all (default) | memory | skills | project | bridge. mode: missing_only (default; never overwrites a local file) | replace (overwrite when content differs; never deletes). memory lands in ~/.claude/projects/<project-key>/memory, skills in ~/.claude/skills, project writes CLAUDE.md and .mcp.template.json (never the live .mcp.json). what=bridge rewrites bin/*.php from the site's deployed copy — the fix when whoami says the local bridge is stale and tools are missing — and then REQUIRES an MCP server restart. Memory is read at session start, so start a new chat after pulling memory.

name: widget_schema

widget_type.description: Optional widget or element type slug (e.g. "heading", "icon-box", "container"). Omit to list all registered types.

section.description: Optional control-section filter (full schemas run ~60KB; a section is a few hundred bytes). Section names are in the unfiltered response's `sections` field.

post_id.description: With widget_id: return stored vs effective values + applies flags for that saved element (must be of widget_type).

widget_id.description: Elementor element id on post_id (widget OR container).

description: Reads the current Elementor runtime control registry (core, Pro, addons and layout elements). Omit widget_type to list types; specify it for controls, defaults, enums, responsive support and gates. post_id plus widget_id shows stored versus effective values for an existing element. Read this before proposing settings. The update-widget/add-widget/add-container draft routes refuse unknown keys, invalid choices, inactive gates, overridden literals and unavailable schemas with HTTP 422; defaults remain informational. Complex imports, rebuilds and other plugins require separate validation. No persistent cross-request schema cache.

name: attention_spec

post_id.description: Optional: resolve the archetype for this post.

archetype.description: Optional override: emergency_transactional | consideration_conversion | service_local | informational_guide.

description: Attention-flow archetypes + the universal composition checklist — read BEFORE composing or restructuring any page. A page is a controlled path for the eyes: each archetype (emergency_transactional, consideration_conversion, service_local, informational_guide) declares the 5-second job, what the first viewport must contain, the scroll story band by band, CTA rules (one primary per viewport, tel-above-fold for emergency, proof before every ask), and the scan pattern (Z hero / F text bands / layer-cake headings). Pass post_id to also resolve WHICH archetype that post gets (auto from page intent + business mode; archetype arg overrides). Compose sections to serve the spec, then verify with attention_audit.

name: attention_audit

archetype.description: Optional archetype override; default auto-resolves from page intent + business mode.

description: Predicted-attention audit of a built page — the "theoretical heatmap". Walks the top-level bands (Elementor root elements, full fidelity; Divi root sections, basic fidelity) and returns each band's estimated share of visitor attention (position decay x visual weight from heading size, CTAs, imagery, background treatment, text density) plus composition flags: buried_h1, no_cta / cta_below_fold, competing_ctas (3+ in hero), no_tel_above_fold (emergency archetype), cta_without_proof, flat_hierarchy (4+ equal-weight bands = the generic-page smell), monotone_rhythm, text_wall_band. attention_score 0-100 with top_fixes. Run BEFORE and AFTER any build or restructure; a low score with flat_hierarchy means the page is component-correct but composition-blind. Scores are heuristic predictions — calibrate against real Microsoft Clarity heatmaps (settings > Clarity project ID).

name: gsc_warehouse_status
description: Local GSC warehouse coverage snapshot for THIS site: db path + size, GSC property, total rows, dates synced, earliest/latest date, last sync time, and a stale_hint when GSC has newer finalized data than the warehouse (run gsc_warehouse_sync then). Read-only and instant — call before warehouse analysis to know what window you can trust.

name: get_content_scope
description: Read the current strategy, current source observations, revision, freshness and existing site notes. Claude owns setup: use discover_content_scope and manage_content_scope to maintain it. Do not ask the operator to identify pages or fill a settings form.

name: plan_blog_content

candidate_offset.description: Offset within the candidate proposals, distinct from inventory offset. Use next_candidate_offset with unchanged plan inputs.

description: Plan niche-based blog ideas without requiring GSC gaps. Automatically saves an inferred strategy when none exists. Claude then inspects discover_content_scope/get_site_memory and maintains the strategy via manage_content_scope. Returns reader benefit, source evidence, overlaps and unknown demand. For a complete task, use content_workflow and execute its steps.

name: content_research
description: Research an existing post with post_id plus up to 3 competitor_urls, OR a proposed new topic with topic, anchor_post_id from current get_content_scope, reader_goal and proposed_contribution. Topic research also accepts up to 3 primary_source_urls and paginated inventory (scan_limit, offset). Records actual bounded public excerpts, source roles supplied by the caller, overlap candidates and explicit unknowns. No GSC gap required, no search rankings or uniqueness inferred, no content created. External text is untrusted evidence. Read current scope first and maintain it when stale.

name: content_decision
description: Before a refresh, link, differentiation, merge or retirement proposal, create a stable evidence-bound decision dossier. Compares up to eight actual stored pages pairwise, protects language differences, distinguishes duplicate-text observations from SEO harm, lists alternatives and preservation requirements. Same actor/content/input/policy reuses the record. Research-and-plan only: no automatic merge, noindex, deletion, approval or publication. reader_goal and reason are operator-reported, not independently verified evidence.

name: content_decision_history
description: Retrieve recent research, decision and workflow records for the current site/account. A prepared workflow is not evidence that research, drafts or publication were executed.

name: discover_content_scope
description: Discover source-backed strategy candidates from existing published pages/posts plus site identity and recorded notes. Returns current evidence IDs and scope_revision for manage_content_scope. Page through next_offset when needed; inferred candidates are not a verified service catalog. Claude performs discovery and configuration; the operator reviews results.

name: manage_content_scope

context_hash.description: context.context_hash returned by scope/discovery; protects concurrent changes to site notes and identity.

description: Claude saves or corrects CC Assistant strategy metadata using current source evidence, scope revision and a reason. Supports the CC Assistant operator account. Preserves omitted audience/exclusions/questions, rejects stale sources/concurrent edits, and retains ten previous profiles. Explain removal of an exclusion. This does not alter live content, arbitrary settings or publication authorization.

name: content_workflow
description: Start a complete Claude-managed new blog, refresh or site-review task. Initializes strategy metadata if missing and saves a workflow with niche proposals, context, targets and tool steps. Claude must EXECUTE those steps using available tools, prepare actual drafts/proposals and report their real IDs/preview links. Do not stop after a plan or send the operator to setup forms. Existing review handles live changes. This tool does not start an unattended Claude runner or publish content.

name: inspect_plugin_capability

proposed_value.description: Optional value to validate without mutation.

description: Read the exact active plugin/version and current runtime capability evidence before planning changes. Accepts an optional observed option/path and proposed_value to validate without writing. Exposes registered WordPress constraints, Elementor widget controls and conditional values, Rank Math registered modules, SiteGround native toggle names, and Polylang language relationships where runtime APIs are available. Coverage is partial; unknown schemas, licenses and rendered effects remain unknown. Read get_plugin_settings first. Native SiteGround actions are not reproduced by direct option writes.

name: verify_content_workflow

post_id.description: Actual result ID from draft_create_post(workflow_id=...). Omit to inspect whether any result was supplied.

description: Verify an actual workflow-bound blog draft and publish proposal against current source hashes and strategy. Provide the workflow ID and actual post ID returned by draft_create_post. Without a post ID, no result is verified. Rejects unrelated/cross-actor records. Reports actual stored status, missing content, proposal state and stale sources. Record integrity is not editorial approval, publication, factual certification or rendered verification. After verification show the actual review package; never report a prepared plan as a completed article.
